1.1: And Shelomoh son of Dawiḏ strengthened himself over his malḵuth, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim was with him and made him exceedingly great.
1.2: And Shelomoh spoke to all Yisra’ĕl, to the commanders of the thousands and of the hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Yisra’ĕl, the heads of the fathers.
1.3: And Shelomoh, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Giḇ’on, for Elohim’s Tent of Appointment was there, which Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had made in the wilderness.
1.4: However, Dawiḏ had brought up the ark of Elohim from Qiryath Ye’arim to the place Dawiḏ had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Yerushalayim.
1.5: And the bronze altar that Betsal’ĕl son of Uri son of Ḥur had made, he put before the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Shelomoh and the assembly sought it.
1.6: And Shelomoh went up there to the bronze altar before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which was at the Tent of Appointment, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
1.7: That night Elohim appeared to Shelomoh, and said to him, “Ask what I should give you.”
1.8: And Shelomoh said to Elohim, “You have shown great kindness to Dawiḏ my father, and have made me meleḵ in his place.
1.9: “Now, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, let Your promise to Dawiḏ my father stand fast, for You have appointed me to reign over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
1.10: “Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I go out and come in before this people. For who rightly rules this great people of Yours?”
1.11: And Elohim said to Shelomoh, “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches or wealth or esteem or the life of your enemies, nor have you asked long life, but have asked wisdom and knowledge for yourself, so as to rightly rule My people over whom I have appointed you to reign,
1.12: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. And riches and wealth and esteem I give you, such as none of the melaḵim have had who have been before you, nor have any after you.”
1.13: And Shelomoh went to Yerushalayim from the high place that was at Giḇ’on, from before the Tent of Appointment, and reigned over Yisra’ĕl.
1.14: And Shelomoh gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the meleḵ in Yerushalayim.
1.15: And the meleḵ made silver and gold to be as stones in Yerushalayim, and he made cedars to be as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country.
1.16: And Shelomoh had horses imported from Mitsrayim and from Quĕ - the meleḵ’s merchants bought them in Quĕ at a price.
1.17: And they came up and brought from Mitsrayim a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty. And so, for all the melaḵim of the Ḥittites and the melaḵim of Aram, they brought them out by their hand.

10.1: And Reḥaḇ’am went to Sheḵem, for all Yisra’ĕl had gone to Sheḵem to appoint him to reign.
10.2: And it came to be, when Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat heard it - he was in Mitsrayim where he had fled from the presence of Shelomoh the meleḵ - that Yaroḇ’am returned from Mitsrayim.
10.3: So they sent for him and called him. And Yaroḇ’am and all Yisra’ĕl came and spoke to Reḥaḇ’am, saying,
10.4: “Your father made our yoke hard, and now, lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put on us, then we shall serve you.”
10.5: And he said to them, “Come back to me after three days.” And the people went.
10.6: Then Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am consulted the elders who stood before his father Shelomoh while he still lived, saying, “What do you advise me to answer these people?”
10.7: And they spoke to him, saying, “If you are good to these people, and shall please them, and speak good words to them, they shall be your servants all the days.”
10.8: But he ignored the advice the elders gave him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
10.9: And he said to them, “What advice do you give? How should we answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke which your father put on us’?”
10.10: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Say this to the people who have spoken to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you make it lighter on us.’ Say this to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
10.11: ‘And now, my father put a heavy yoke on you, but I, I add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I with scourges!’ ”
10.12: So Yaroḇ’am and all the people came to Reḥaḇ’am on the third day, as the meleḵ commanded, saying, “Come back to me the third day.”
10.13: And the meleḵ answered them harshly. Thus Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am ignored the advice of the elders,
10.14: and spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I, I add to it; my father chastised you with whips, but I with scourges!”
10.15: So the meleḵ did not listen to the people, for the turn of events was from Elohim, in order for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to establish His word, which He had spoken by the hand of Aḥiyahu the Shilonite to Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat.
10.16: And when all Yisra’ĕl saw that the meleḵ did not listen to them, the people answered the meleḵ, saying, “What portion have we in Dawiḏ? And we have no inheritance in the son of Yishai. Every man to your mighty ones, O Yisra’ĕl! Now see to your own house, O Dawiḏ!” So all Yisra’ĕl went to their tents.
10.17: But as for the children of Yisra’ĕl who dwelt in the cities of Yahuḏah, Reḥaḇ’am reigned over them.
10.18: Then Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am sent Haḏoram, who was over the compulsory labor, and the children of Yisra’ĕl stoned him with stones, and he died. And Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am hastily mounted his chariot to flee to Yerushalayim.
10.19: Thus Yisra’ĕl revolted against the house of Dawiḏ to this day.

11.1: And when Reḥaḇ’am came to Yerushalayim, he assembled from the house of Yahuḏah and Binyamin one hundred and eighty thousand men of battle to fight against Yisra’ĕl, to bring back the reign to Reḥaḇ’am.
11.2: But the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Shemayahu the man of Elohim, saying,
11.3: “Speak to Reḥaḇ’am son of Shelomoh, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and to all Yisra’ĕl in Yahuḏah and Binyamin, saying,
11.4: ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do no go up or fight against your brothers! Let every man return to his house, for this matter is from Me.” ’ ” So they obeyed the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and turned back from going against Yaroḇ’am.
11.5: And Reḥaḇ’am dwelt in Yerushalayim, and built cities for a defense in Yahuḏah.
11.6: And he built Bĕyth Leḥem, and Ĕytam, and Teqowa,
11.7: and Bĕyth Tsur, and Soḵo, and Aḏullam,
11.8: and Gath, and Marĕshah, and Ziph,
11.9: and Aḏorayim, and Laḵish, and Azĕqah,
11.10: and Tsor’ah, and Ayalon, and Ḥeḇron, which are in Yahuḏah and Binyamin, cities of defense.
11.11: And he strengthened the strongholds, and put commanders in them, and stores of food, and oil, and wine,
11.12: and shields and spears in every city, and made them very strong. Thus Yahuḏah and Binyamin were his.
11.13: And from all their borders the kohenim and the Lĕwites who were in all Yisra’ĕl took their stand with him.
11.14: For the Lĕwites left their open lands and their possessions and came to Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, for Yaroḇ’am and his sons had rejected them from serving as kohenim unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
11.15: as he appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for demons, and the calf idols which he had made.
11.16: And after the Lĕwites left, those from all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, such as applied their heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, came to Yerushalayim to offer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.
11.17: And they strengthened the malḵuth of Yahuḏah, and made Reḥaḇ’am son of Shelomoh strong for three years, for they walked in the way of Dawiḏ and Shelomoh for three years.
11.18: And Reḥaḇ’am took for himself as wife Maḥalath the daughter of Yerimoth son of Dawiḏ, and of Aḇiḥayil the daughter of Eliyaḇ son of Yishai.
11.19: And she bore him sons: Ye’ush, and Shemaryah, and Zaham.
11.20: And after her he took Ma’aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇshalom. And she bore him Aḇiyah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.
11.21: And Reḥaḇ’am loved Ma’aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇshalom more than all his wives and his concubines. For he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and brought forth twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
11.22: And Reḥaḇ’am appointed Aḇiyah son of Ma’aḵah as chief, to be leader among his brothers, in order to make him reign.
11.23: And he had understanding, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the lands of Yahuḏah and Binyamin, to all the cities of defense, and gave them ample provision. And he sought many wives.

12.1: And it came to be, when Reḥaḇ’am had established the malḵuth and had strengthened himself, that he forsook the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and all Yisra’ĕl with him.
12.2: And it came to be, in the fifth year of Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am, that Shishaq meleḵ of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim - because they had trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 -
12.3: with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horsemen, and innumerable people who came with him out of Mitsrayim: the Luḇim, the Sukkites and the Kushites.
12.4: And he took the cities of defense of Yahuḏah and came to Yerushalayim.
12.5: And Shemayah the naḇi came to Reḥaḇ’am and the rulers of Yahuḏah, who had been gathered in Yerushalayim because of Shishaq, and said to them, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘You have forsaken Me, and therefore I also have left you in the hand of Shishaq.’ ”
12.6: Then the rulers of Yisra’ĕl and the meleḵ humbled themselves, and they said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is righteous.”
12.7: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saw that they humbled themselves, the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Shemayah, saying, “They have humbled themselves. I do not destroy them, but I shall give to them some deliverance, and not pour out My wrath on Yerushalayim by the hand of Shishaq,
12.8: but they are to become his servants, so that they know My service and the service of the reigns of the lands.”
12.9: And Shishaq meleḵ of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim, and took away the treasures of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the treasures of the meleḵ’s house. He took all, he also took the gold shields which Shelomoh had made.
12.10: And Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am made bronze shields to replace them and committed them into the hands of the chiefs of the guard, who guarded the entrance of the meleḵ’s house.
12.11: And it came to be, whenever the meleḵ went into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the guard would go and bring them out, then they would take them back into the guardroom.
12.12: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turned from him, so as not to destroy him completely. And matters also went well in Yahuḏah.
12.13: So Meleḵ Reḥaḇ’am strengthened himself in Yerushalayim and reigned. For Reḥaḇ’am was forty-one years old when he became meleḵ, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, to put His Name there. And his mother’s name was Na’amah, the Ammonitess.
12.14: And he did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.15: And the acts of Reḥaḇ’am, the first and the last, are they not written in the book of Shemayah the naḇi, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ’am and Yaroḇ’am all the days.
12.16: So Reḥaḇ’am slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Dawiḏ. And Aḇiyah his son reigned in his place.

13.1: In the eighteenth year of Meleḵ Yaroḇ’am, Aḇiyah began to reign over Yahuḏah.
13.2: He reigned three years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Miḵayahu the daughter of Uri’ĕl of Giḇ’ah. And there was fighting between Aḇiyah and Yaroḇ’am.
13.3: And Aḇiyah joined the battle with an army of mighty men of battle, four hundred thousand choice men. And Yaroḇ’am drew up in battle formation against him with eight hundred thousand choice men, mighty brave men.
13.4: And Aḇiyah stood on Mount Tsemarayim, which is in the mountains of Ephrayim, and said, “Hear me, Yaroḇ’am and all Yisra’ĕl:
13.5: “Do you not know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl has given the reign over Yisra’ĕl to Dawiḏ forever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt?
13.6: “Yet Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, the servant of Shelomoh son of Dawiḏ, rose up and rebelled against his master.
13.7: “And vain men gathered to him, sons of Beliya’al, and strengthened themselves against Reḥaḇ’am son of Shelomoh, when Reḥaḇ’am was young and tender of heart and could not stand against them.
13.8: “And now you think to stand against the reign of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which is in the hand of the sons of Dawiḏ. And you are a large crowd, and with you are the gold calves which Yaroḇ’am made for you as mighty ones.
13.9: “Have you not thrown out the kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the sons of Aharon, and the Lĕwites, and made for yourselves priests, like the peoples of the lands, so that whoever comes to ordain himself with a young bull and seven rams then becomes a priest of non-mighty ones?
13.10: “But as for us, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is our Elohim, and we have not forsaken Him, and kohenim are serving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the sons of Aharon and the Lĕwites, in the work,
13.11: and are burning to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 every morning and every evening burnt offerings and sweet incense, and the showbread is put on the clean table, and the lampstand of gold with its lamps to burn every evening, for we are guarding the Charge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim. But you have forsaken Him.
13.12: “And see, with us as Head is Elohim Himself, and His kohenim with sounding trumpets to sound the alarm against you. O children of Yisra’ĕl, do not fight against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers, for you are not going to prosper!”
13.13: But Yaroḇ’am sent round an ambush to go behind them, so they were in front of Yahuḏah, and the ambush was behind them.
13.14: And Yahuḏah turned and saw the battle was both in front and behind them. Then they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the kohenim sounded the trumpets.
13.15: And the men of Yahuḏah gave a shout. And it came to be, as the men of Yahuḏah shouted, that Elohim smote Yaroḇ’am and all Yisra’ĕl before Aḇiyah and Yahuḏah.
13.16: And the children of Yisra’ĕl fled before Yahuḏah, and Elohim gave them into their hand.
13.17: And Aḇiyah and his people smote them with a great smiting, and five hundred thousand choice men of Yisra’ĕl fell slain.
13.18: And the children of Yisra’ĕl were humbled at that time, while the children of Yahuḏah prevailed, because they relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.
13.19: And Aḇiyah pursued Yaroḇ’am and captured cities from him: Bĕyth Ĕl with its villages, and Yeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
13.20: And Yaroḇ’am did not regain power again in the days of Aḇiyahu. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote him, and he died.
13.21: But Aḇiyah grew strong, and took fourteen wives, and brought forth twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
13.22: And the rest of the acts of Aḇiyah, and his ways, and his words are written in the commentary of the naḇi Iddo.

14.1: So Aḇiyah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Dawiḏ. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land rested ten years.
14.2: And Asa did what was good and what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim,
14.3: and removed the altars of the stranger, and the high places, and broke down the pillars and cut down the Ashĕrim,
14.4: and commanded Yahuḏah to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers, and to do the Torah and the Command.
14.5: And he removed the high places and the sun-pillars from all the cities of Yahuḏah, and the reign rested under him.
14.6: And he built cities of defense in Yahuḏah, since the land had rest and he had no fighting in those years, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had given him rest.
14.7: And he said to Yahuḏah, “Let us build these cities and make walls around them, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us, because we have sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim. We have sought, and He has given us rest all around.” So they built and prospered.
14.8: And Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Yahuḏah bearing shields and spears, and from Binyamin two hundred and eighty thousand men bearing shields and drew bows. All of them were mighty brave men.
14.9: And Zeraḥ the Kushite came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came to Marĕshah.
14.10: And Asa went out against him, and they prepared in battle array in the Valley of Tsephathah at Marĕshah.
14.11: And Asa called to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, there is no one but You to help between the mighty and the powerless. Help us, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, for we rest on You, and in Your Name we go against this crowd. O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are our Elohim, do not let man prevail against You!”
14.12: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote the Kushites before Asa and Yahuḏah, and the Kushites fled.
14.13: And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Gerar. And the Kushites fell, until none was left alive for them, for they were broken before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His army. And they took very much spoil,
14.14: and smote all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon them. And they plundered all the cities, for there was exceedingly much spoil in them.
14.15: And they also smote the camps of the herdsmen, and captured many sheep and camels, and returned to Yerushalayim.

15.1: And the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon Azaryahu son of Oḏĕḏ.
15.2: And he went out to face Asa, and said to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Yahuḏah and Binyamin. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with you while you are with Him. And if you seek Him, He is found by you, but if you forsake Him, He forsakes you.
15.3: “And for many days Yisra’ĕl has been without the true Elohim, and without a Torah kohĕn, and without Torah.
15.4: “But in their distress they turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and they sought Him, and He was found by them.
15.5: “And in those days there was no peace to the one who went out, nor to the one who came in, for great disturbances were on all the inhabitants of the lands,
15.6: and they were beaten down, nation by nation, and city by city, for Elohim troubled them with every distress.
15.7: “But you, be strong and do not let your hands be feeble, for there is a reward for your work!”
15.8: And when Asa heard these words and the neḇuah of Oḏĕḏ the naḇi, he took courage, and removed the abominations from all the land of Yahuḏah and Binyamin and from the cities which he had taken in the mountains of Ephrayim, and restored the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that was before the porch of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
15.9: and gathered all Yahuḏah and Binyamin, and those who sojourned with them from Ephrayim, and Menashsheh, and Shim’on, for they came over to him in great numbers from Yisra’ĕl when they saw that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim was with him.
15.10: And they gathered together at Yerushalayim in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa,
15.11: and offered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on that day seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep from the spoil which they had brought.
15.12: And they entered into a covenant to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers with all their heart and with all their being;
15.13: and whoever would not seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl would be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman.
15.14: And they swore to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with a loud voice, with shouting and with trumpets and with rams’ horns.
15.15: And all Yahuḏah rejoiced concerning the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought Him with all their being. And He was found by them, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave them rest all around.
15.16: And he also removed Ma’aḵah, the mother of Asa the meleḵ, from being queen mother, because she had made an abominable image of Ashĕrah. And Asa cut down her abominable image, and crushed it, and burned it by the wadi Qiḏron.
15.17: Yet the high places were not removed from Yisra’ĕl. However, the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
15.18: And he brought into the House of Elohim the qodesh items of his father and his own qodesh items: silver and gold and utensils.
15.19: And there was no more fighting until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

16.1: In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Ba’asha the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl came up against Yahuḏah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone going out or coming in to Asa, meleḵ of Yahuḏah.
16.2: And Asa brought silver and gold from the treasuries of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and of the meleḵ’s house, and sent to Ben-Haḏaḏ meleḵ of Aram, who dwelt in Darmeseq, saying,
16.3: “Let there be a covenant between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Ba’asha meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, so that he withdraws from me.”
16.4: And Ben-Haḏaḏ listened to Meleḵ Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Yisra’ĕl, and they smote Iyon, and Dan, and Aḇĕl Mayim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
16.5: And it came to be, when Ba’asha heard it, that he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.
16.6: Then Asa the meleḵ brought all Yahuḏah, and they took away the stones and timber of Ramah, which Ba’asha had used for building. And with them he built Geḇa and Mitspah.
16.7: And at that time Ḥanani the seer came to Asa meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and said to him, “Because you have relied on the meleḵ of Aram, and have not relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, therefore the army of the meleḵ of Aram has escaped from your hand.
16.8: “Were the Kushites and the Luḇim not a mighty army with very many chariots and horsemen? And because you relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He gave them into your hand.
16.9: “For the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 diligently search throughout all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is perfect to Him. You have acted foolishly in this, so from now on you shall have battles.”
16.10: And Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in prison, enraged at him because of this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.
16.11: And look, the acts of Asa, the first and the last, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah and Yisra’ĕl.
16.12: And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his disease was severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but the physicians.
16.13: So Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
16.14: And they buried him in his own tomb, which he had made for himself in the City of Dawiḏ. And they laid him in the bed which was filled with spices and various kinds of ointments mixed by the perfumer’s skill. And they made a very great burning for him.

17.1: And Yahoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and strengthened himself against Yisra’ĕl,
17.2: and placed an army in all the walled cities of Yahuḏah, and put watch-posts in the land of Yahuḏah and in the cities of Ephrayim which Asa his father had taken.
17.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with Yahoshaphat, for he walked in the former ways of his father Dawiḏ, and did not seek the Ba’als,
17.4: but sought the Elohim of his father, and walked in His Commands and not according to the deeds of Yisra’ĕl.
17.5: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 established the reign in his hand. And all Yahuḏah gave presents to Yahoshaphat, and he had great riches and esteem.
17.6: And his heart was exalted in the Ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and he again removed the high places and the Ashĕrim from Yahuḏah.
17.7: And in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders, Ben-Ḥayil, and Oḇaḏyah, and Zeḵaryah, and Nethan’ĕl, and Miḵayahu, to teach in the cities of Yahuḏah.
17.8: And with them he sent Lĕwites: Shemayahu, and Nethanyahu, and Zeḇaḏyahu, and Asah’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yahonathan, and Aḏoniyahu, and Toḇiyahu, and Toḇaḏoniyah, the Lĕwites, and with them Elishama and Yahoram, the kohenim.
17.9: And they taught in Yahuḏah, and with them was the Book of the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they went around into all the cities of Yahuḏah and taught the people.
17.10: And the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell on all the reigns of the lands that were around Yahuḏah, and they did not fight against Yahoshaphat.
17.11: And some of the Pelishtites brought Yahoshaphat gifts and a load of silver. And the Araḇians brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
17.12: And Yahoshaphat became increasingly great, and he built palaces and storage cities in Yahuḏah.
17.13: And he had much work in the cities of Yahuḏah. And the men of battle, mighty brave men, were in Yerushalayim.
17.14: And these were their numbers, according to their fathers’ houses: Of Yahuḏah, the commanders of thousands: Aḏnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty brave men;
17.15: and next to him was Yahoḥanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
17.16: and next to him was Amasyah son of Ziḵri, who volunteered himself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and with him two hundred thousand mighty brave men.
17.17: And of Binyamin: Elyaḏa, a mighty brave one, and with him two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield;
17.18: and next to him was Yahozaḇaḏ, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand prepared for battle.
17.19: These were the ones serving the meleḵ, besides those whom the meleḵ put in the walled cities throughout all Yahuḏah.

18.1: And Yahoshaphat had great riches and esteem, and allied himself with Aḥaḇ by marriage.
18.2: And some years later he went down to visit Aḥaḇ in Shomeron. And Aḥaḇ slaughtered many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and incited him to go up with him to Ramoth Gil’aḏ.
18.3: And Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said to Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah, “Do you go with me against Ramoth Gil’aḏ?” And he answered him, “I am as you are, and my people as your people, even with you in battle.”
18.4: And Yahoshaphat said to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, “Please inquire for the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 today.”
18.5: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl gathered the neḇi’im together, four hundred men, and said to them, “Do we go against Ramoth Gil’aḏ to battle, or do I refrain?” And they said, “Go up, for Elohim gives it into the meleḵ’s hand.”
18.6: But Yahoshaphat said, “Is there not still a naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 here, so that we inquire of him?”
18.7: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said to Yahoshaphat, “There is still one man to inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from him; but I hate him, because he never naḇa good concerning me, but always evil. He is Miḵayahu, the son of Yimla.” And Yahoshaphat said, “Let not the meleḵ say so!”
18.8: So the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl called one of his officers and said, “Bring Miḵayahu son of Yimla at once!”
18.9: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl and Yahoshaphat the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, dressed in their robes, sat each on his throne. And they sat at a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomeron. And all the neḇi’im naḇu before them.
18.10: And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena’anah had made horns of iron for himself, and said, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘With these you push the Arameans until they are destroyed.’ ”
18.11: And all the neḇi’im naḇu so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gil’aḏ and prosper, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give it into the hand of the meleḵ.”
18.12: And the messenger who had gone to call Miḵayahu spoke to him, saying, “See, the words of the neḇi’im with one mouth are good towards the meleḵ. So please let your word be like the word of one of them, and you shall speak good.”
18.13: And Miḵayahu said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, whatever my Elohim says, that I speak.”
18.14: And he came to the meleḵ. And the meleḵ said to him, “Miḵayahu, do we go against Ramoth Gil’aḏ to battle, or do I refrain?” And he said, “Go and prosper, and they are given into your hand!”
18.15: And the meleḵ said to him, “How many times have I made you swear that you do not speak to me, except the truth, in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
18.16: So he said, “I saw all Yisra’ĕl scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his house in peace.’ ”
18.17: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said to Yahoshaphat, “Did I not say to you that he would not naḇa good concerning me, but evil?”
18.18: Then he said, “Therefore hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: I saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sitting on His throne, and all the host of the shamayim standing on His right and on His left.
18.19: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, ‘Who shall entice Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl to go up and fall at Ramoth Gil’aḏ?’ And one said this, and another said that.
18.20: “And a spirit came forward and stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, ‘Let me entice him.’ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, ‘In what way?’
18.21: “And he said, ‘I shall go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his neḇi’im.’ And He said, ‘Entice him, and also prevail. Go out and do so.’
18.22: “And now, see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of these neḇi’im of yours, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken evil concerning you.”
18.23: And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena’anah came near and smote Miḵayahu on the cheek, and said, “Which way did the spirit of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 pass over from me to speak to you?”
18.24: And Miḵayahu said, “Look, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide!”
18.25: Then the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said, “Take Miḵayahu, and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Yo’ash the meleḵ’s son,
18.26: and say, ‘Thus said the meleḵ, “Put this one in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.” ’ ”
18.27: And Miḵayahu said, “If you return at all in peace, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Hear, all you people!”
18.28: Then the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl and Yahoshaphat the meleḵ of Yahuḏah went up to Ramoth Gil’aḏ.
18.29: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said to Yahoshaphat, “Let me disguise myself and go into battle, but you put on your robes.” And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl disguised himself, and they went into battle.
18.30: And the meleḵ of Aram had commanded the commanders of the chariots who were with him, saying, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.”
18.31: And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw Yahoshaphat, that they said, “It is the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl!” So they turned around to fight against him, and Yahoshaphat cried out, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 helped him, and Elohim moved them to turn away from him.
18.32: And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, that they turned back from pursuing him.
18.33: And a man drew a bow in his simplicity, and smote the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl between the joints of his armor. And he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded.”
18.34: But the battle increased that day, and the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening, and he died at the time of the going down of the sun.

19.1: And Yahoshaphat the meleḵ of Yahuḏah returned to his house in peace in Yerushalayim.
19.2: And Yahu son of Ḥanani the seer went out to face him, and said to Meleḵ Yahoshaphat, “Do you help the wicked and love those who hate 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Therefore the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon you.
19.3: “But good matters are found in you, in that you have removed the Ashĕroth from the land, and have prepared your heart to seek Elohim.”
19.4: So Yahoshaphat dwelt in Yerushalayim, and he went out again among the people from Be’ĕrsheḇa to the hill country of Ephrayim, and brought them back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.
19.5: And he appointed judges in the land in all the walled cities of Yahuḏah, city by city,
19.6: and said to the judges, “Watch what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is with you in the matter of right-ruling.
19.7: “And now, let the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be upon you. Guard and do it, for there is no unrighteousness with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim nor partiality, nor taking of bribes.”
19.8: And in Yerushalayim Yahoshaphat also appointed some of the Lĕwites and kohenim, and some of the chief fathers of Yisra’ĕl, for the right-ruling of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and for dispute. Then they returned to Yerushalayim.
19.9: And he commanded them, saying, “Do this in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, trustworthy and with a perfect heart:
19.10: “When any dispute comes to you from your brothers who dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between Torah and Command, Laws and Right-Rulings, then you shall warn them, lest they trespass against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and wrath come upon you and your brothers. Do this, and you shall not be guilty.
19.11: “And look, Amaryahu the chief kohĕn is over you in all matters of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Zeḇaḏyahu son of Yishma’ĕl, the ruler of the house of Yahuḏah, for all the matters of the meleḵ, and the Lĕwites are officials before you. Be strong and do, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with the good.”

2.1: And Shelomoh gave word to build a House for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and a house for his malḵuth.
2.2: Then Shelomoh enrolled seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand hewing in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
2.3: And Shelomoh sent to Ḥuram meleḵ of Tsor, saying, “As you did for my father Dawiḏ, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in -
2.4: see, I am building a House for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, to qadosh it to Him, to burn before Him sweet incense, and for the continual showbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Shabbathoth, and on the New Moons, and on the Appointed Times of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim. This is for Yisra’ĕl forever.
2.5: “And the House which I build is great, for our Elohim is greater than all mighty ones.
2.6: “But who is able to build Him a House, since the shamayim and the shamayim of the shamayim are unable to contain Him? Who am I then, that I should build Him a House, except to offer before Him?
2.7: “And now, send me at once a man who knows to work in gold, and in silver, and in bronze, and in iron, and in purple and crimson and blue, and knowing to engrave with the skilled men who are with me in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, whom Dawiḏ my father has prepared.
2.8: “And send me cedar, cypress and algum logs from Leḇanon, for I know that your servants know to cut timber in Leḇanon. And see, my servants are with your servants,
2.9: even to prepare plenty of timber for me, for the House that I am building is great and marvelous.
2.10: “And see, I have given servants to you, the hewers who cut timber, twenty thousand kors of ground wheat, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
2.11: Then Ḥuram the meleḵ of Tsor answered in writing, which he sent to Shelomoh, “Because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loves His people, He has made you meleḵ over them.”
2.12: And Ḥuram said, “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, who made the shamayim and earth, for He has given Meleḵ Dawiḏ a wise son, knowing wisdom and understanding, to build a House for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and a house for his malḵuth!
2.13: “And now I have sent a skilled man having understanding, Ḥuram-aḇi,
2.14: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tsor, who knows to work in gold, and in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stone, and in wood, purple and blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson, and to make any engraving and to accomplish any plan that is given to him, with your skilled men and with the skilled men of my master Dawiḏ your father.
2.15: “And now, the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine which my master has spoken of, let him send to his servants.
2.16: “And let us cut wood from Leḇanon, as much as you need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Yapho, and you take it up to Yerushalayim.”
2.17: And Shelomoh numbered all the men, the strangers who were in the land of Yisra’ĕl, according to the census in which Dawiḏ his father had numbered them, and they were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
2.18: And he made seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, and eighty thousand hewers in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers to make the people work.

20.1: And after this it came to be that the children of Mo’aḇ and the children of Ammon came in, and with them some of the peoples, against Yahoshaphat to battle.
20.2: And they came and spoke to Yahoshaphat, saying, “A great army is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. And see, they are in Ḥatsetson Tamar,” which is Ĕyn Geḏi.
20.3: And Yahoshaphat was afraid, and turned his face to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yahuḏah.
20.4: And Yahuḏah gathered to inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even from all the cities of Yahuḏah they came to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.5: And Yahoshaphat stood in the assembly of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in front of the new courtyard,
20.6: and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of our fathers, are You not Elohim in the shamayim, and do You not rule over all the reigns of the nations, and in Your hand is there not power and might, so that no one is able to stand against You?
20.7: “Are You not our Elohim? You have driven out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Yisra’ĕl, and gave it to the seed of Aḇraham whom you love forever.
20.8: “And they dwell in it, and have built You a Miqdash in it for Your Name, saying,
20.9: ‘If evil comes upon us, such as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or scarcity of food, we shall stand before this House and in Your presence - for Your Name is in this House - and cry out to You in our distress, and You do hear and save.’
20.10: “And now, see, the children of Ammon and Mo’aḇ, and Mount Sĕ’ir, whom You would not let Yisra’ĕl invade when they came out of the land of Mitsrayim, for they turned from them and did not destroy them,
20.11: and see, they are repaying us by coming in to drive us out of Your possession which You have given us to inherit.
20.12: “O our Elohim, would You not judge them? For we are powerless against this great army that is coming against us. And we do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
20.13: And all Yahuḏah, with their little ones, their wives, and their children, stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.14: And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon Yaḥazi’ĕl son of Zeḵaryahu, son of Benayah, son of Ye’i’ĕl, son of Mattanyah, a Lĕwite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly,
20.15: and he said, “Listen, all Yahuḏah, and you inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and Meleḵ Yahoshaphat! Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to you, ‘Do not fear, nor be afraid of the face of this great army, for the battle is not yours, but Elohim’s.
20.16: ‘Go down against them tomorrow. See, they are coming up by the ascent of Tsits, and you shall find them at the end of the wadi before the Wilderness of Yeru’ĕl.
20.17: ‘It is not for you to fight in this. Position yourselves, stand still and see the deliverance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with you, O Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim!’ Do not be afraid nor fear, go out against them tomorrow, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with you.”
20.18: And Yahoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fell down before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to bow themselves before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.19: And the Lĕwites, of the children of the Qehathites and of the children of the Qorḥites stood up to praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl with an exceedingly loud voice.
20.20: And they rose early in the morning and went out into the Wilderness of Teqowa. And as they went out, Yahoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Yahuḏah and you inhabitants of Yerushalayim: Trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and be steadfast, trust His neḇi’im and prosper.”
20.21: And after consulting with the people, he appointed those who should sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and who should praise the splendor of qodeshah, as they went out before the army and were saying, “Give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for His kindness is everlasting.”
20.22: And when they began singing and praising, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 laid ambushes against the children of Ammon, Mo’aḇ, and Mount Sĕ’ir, who had come against Yahuḏah, and they were smitten.
20.23: Then the children of Ammon and Mo’aḇ stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Sĕ’ir to destroy and annihilate them. And when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Sĕ’ir, they helped to destroy one another.
20.24: And when Yahuḏah came at the lookout in the wilderness, they looked toward the army and saw their dead bodies, lying on the ground, and none had escaped.
20.25: And Yahoshaphat and his people came to take away their spoil, and they found among them a great amount of valuables on the dead bodies, and precious jewelry, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could take away. And they were three days plundering the spoil, for it was much.
20.26: And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beraḵah, for there they baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Therefore the name of that place was called The Valley of Beraḵah to this day.
20.27: Then they returned, every man of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, with Yahoshaphat in front of them, to go back to Yerushalayim with joy, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had made them rejoice over their enemies.
20.28: And they came to Yerushalayim, with harps and lyres and trumpets, to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.29: And the fear of Elohim was on all the reigns of the lands when they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had fought against the enemies of Yisra’ĕl.
20.30: Then the malḵuth of Yahoshaphat was at peace, for his Elohim gave him rest on all sides.
20.31: Thus Yahoshaphat reigned over Yahuḏah - thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Azuḇah the daughter of Shilḥi.
20.32: And he walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.33: Only, the high places were not taken away, for as yet the people had not prepared their hearts for the Elohim of their fathers.
20.34: And the rest of the acts of Yahoshaphat, the first and the last see, they are written in the book of Yahu son of Ḥanani, which is mentioned in the book of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
20.35: And after this Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah joined himself with Aḥazyahu meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl. He did wickedness in doing so.
20.36: And he joined himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Etsyon Geḇer.
20.37: Then Eli’ezer son of Doḏawahu of Marĕshah naḇu against Yahoshaphat, saying, “Because you have joined yourself with Aḥazyahu, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall break up your work.” And the ships were wrecked, so that they were unable to go to Tarshish.

21.1: And Yahoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ. And Yahoram his son reigned in his place.
21.2: And he had brothers, the sons of Yahoshaphat: Azaryahu, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Zeḵaryahu, and Azaryahu, and Miḵa’ĕl, and Shephatyahu. All these were sons of Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
21.3: And their father gave them many gifts of silver and gold and precious items, with walled cities in Yahuḏah, but he had given the reign to Yahoram because he was the first-born.
21.4: And when Yahoram had risen up over the reign of his father and made himself strong, he slew all his brothers with the sword, and also others of the heads of Yisra’ĕl.
21.5: Yahoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
21.6: And he walked in the way of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl, as the house of Aḥaḇ had done, for he had the daughter of Aḥaḇ as a wife. And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.7: However, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not destroy the house of Dawiḏ, because of the covenant He had made with Dawiḏ, and since He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons, all the days.
21.8: In his days the Eḏomites revolted from under the hand of Yahuḏah, and appointed a meleḵ over themselves.
21.9: Then Yahoram went out with his officers, and all his chariots with him. And it came to be that he rose by night and smote the Eḏomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.
21.10: Thus the Eḏomites revolted from under the hand of Yahuḏah to this day. Then Liḇnah revolted from under his hand, because he had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of his fathers.
21.11: He had also made high places in the mountains of Yahuḏah, and caused the inhabitants of Yerushalayim to commit whoring, and led Yahuḏah astray.
21.12: And a letter came to him from Ĕliyahu the naḇi, saying, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your father Dawiḏ, ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Yahoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa meleḵ of Yahuḏah,
21.13: but have walked in the way of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl, and have made Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim to commit whoring like the whorings of the house of Aḥaḇ, and also have slain your brothers, those of your father’s household, who were better than yourself,
21.14: see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is going to strike with a great blow among your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions,
21.15: and you, with many sicknesses, with disease of your intestines, until your intestines come out because of the sickness, day by day.’ ”
21.16: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stirred up the spirit of the Pelishtites against Yahoram, and of the Araḇians who were near the Kushites.
21.17: And they came up into Yahuḏah and broke into it, and captured all the possessions that were found in the meleḵ’s house, and also his sons and his wives, so that there was not a son left to him except Yaho’aḥaz, the youngest of his sons.
21.18: And after all this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 plagued him in his intestines with a disease for which there was no healing.
21.19: And it came to be in the course of time, at the end of two years, that his intestines came out because of his sickness, and he died in great pain. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning for his fathers.
21.20: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim, and passed away without pleasantries. And they buried him in the City of Dawiḏ, but not in the tombs of the melaḵim.

22.1: And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim appointed Aḥazyahu his youngest son to reign in his place, for the raiding band that came with the Araḇians into the camp had slain all the older sons. So Aḥazyahu son of Yahoram, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, reigned.
22.2: Aḥazyahu was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim one year. And his mother’s name was Athalyahu the granddaughter of Omri.
22.3: He too walked in the ways of the house of Aḥaḇ, for his mother counselled him to do wickedly.
22.4: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, like the house of Aḥaḇ, for they were his counsellors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
22.5: He also walked in their counsel, and went with Yahoram son of Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl to fight against Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram at Ramoth Gil’aḏ. And the Arameans smote Yoram,
22.6: and he returned to Yizre’ĕl to recover from the wounds which he had received at Ramah, when he fought against Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram. And Azaryahu son of Yahoram, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, went down to see Yahoram son of Aḥaḇ in Yizre’ĕl, for he was sick.
22.7: But from Elohim came the downfall of Aḥazyahu, through his coming to Yoram. For when he came he went out with Yahoram against Yahu son of Nimshi, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had anointed to cut off the house of Aḥaḇ.
22.8: And it came to be, when Yahu was executing judgment on the house of Aḥaḇ, that he found the rulers of Yahuḏah and the sons of Aḥazyahu’s brothers who served Aḥazyahu, and slew them.
22.9: So he searched for Aḥazyahu, and they caught him while he was hiding in Shomeron, and brought him to Yahu, and put him to death, then buried him, for they said, “He is the son of Yahoshaphat, who sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all his heart.” And there was none in the house of Aḥazyahu strong enough to reign.
22.10: And when Athalyahu the mother of Aḥazyahu saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed all the offspring of the reign of the house of Yahuḏah.
22.11: But Yahoshaḇ’ath, the daughter of the meleḵ, took Yo’ash son of Aḥazyahu, and stole him away from among the meleḵ’s sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So Yahoshaḇ’ath, the daughter of Meleḵ Yahoram, the wife of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn, because she was the sister of Aḥazyahu, hid him from Athalyahu so that she could not put him to death.
22.12: And he was hidden with them in the House of Elohim for six years, while Athalyahu was reigning over the land.

23.1: And in the seventh year Yahoyaḏa strengthened himself, and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds: Azaryahu son of Yeroḥam, and Yishma’ĕl son of Yahoḥanan, and Azaryahu son of Oḇĕḏ, and Ma’asĕyahu son of Aḏayah, and Elishaphat son of Ziḵri.
23.2: And they went about through Yahuḏah and gathered the Lĕwites from all the cities of Yahuḏah, and the chiefs of the fathers of Yisra’ĕl, and they came to Yerushalayim.
23.3: And all the assembly made a covenant with the meleḵ in the House of Elohim. And he said to them, “See, the son of the meleḵ is to reign, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said of the sons of Dawiḏ.
23.4: “This is what you do: One-third of you entering on the Shabbath, of the kohenim and the Lĕwites, gatekeepers of the thresholds;
23.5: and one-third are at the meleḵ’s house, and one-third at the Gate of the Foundation, while all the people are in the courtyards of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.6: “And let no one come into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 except the kohenim and those of the Lĕwites who serve - they go in, for they are qodesh. But all the people are to guard the Charge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.7: “And the Lĕwites shall surround the meleḵ on all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand. And whoever comes into the House, let him be put to death. And be with the meleḵ when he comes in and when he goes out.”
23.8: And the Lĕwites and all Yahuḏah did according to all that Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn commanded. And each man took his men who were to come in on the Shabbath, with those going out on the Shabbath, for Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn did not dismiss the divisions.
23.9: And Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the large and small shields which had been Meleḵ Dawiḏ’s, that were in the House of Elohim.
23.10: And he stood all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the House to the left side of the House, along by the altar and by the House, all around the meleḵ.
23.11: And they brought out the son of the meleḵ and put on him the diadem and the Witness, and appointed him to reign. Then Yahoyaḏa and his sons anointed him, and said, “Let the meleḵ live!”
23.12: And Athalyahu heard the noise of the people running and praising the meleḵ, and she came to the people in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
23.13: and looked and saw the meleḵ standing by his column at the entrance. And the chiefs and the trumpeters were beside the meleḵ, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, also the singers with instruments of song, and those who led in praise. Then Athalyahu tore her garments and said, “Treason! Treason!”
23.14: And Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn brought out the commanders of hundreds who were put over the army, and said to them, “Take her outside the ranks, and slay with the sword whoever follows her.” For the kohĕn said, “Do not kill her in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
23.15: So they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the entrance of the Horse Gate into the meleḵ’s house, and they put her to death there.
23.16: Yahoyaḏa then made a covenant - between himself and the people and the meleḵ - to be the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.17: And all the people went to the house of Ba’al, and broke it down. They completely broke up its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Ba’al before the altars.
23.18: And Yahoyaḏa put the offices of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 into the hand of the kohenim, the Lĕwites, whom Dawiḏ had assigned in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to offer the burnt offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, with rejoicing and with singing, by the hands of Dawiḏ.
23.19: And he stood the gatekeepers at the gates of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so that no one who was in any way unclean should enter.
23.20: And he took the commanders of hundreds, and the nobles, and the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the meleḵ down from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they went through the Upper Gate to the meleḵ’s house, and placed the meleḵ on the throne of the reign.
23.21: And all the people of the land rejoiced. And the city had rest, for they had slain Athalyahu with the sword.

24.1: Yo’ash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. And the name of his mother was Tsiḇyah of Be’ĕrsheḇa.
24.2: And Yo’ash did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all the days of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn.
24.3: And Yahoyaḏa took for him two wives, and he brought forth sons and daughters.
24.4: And after this it came to be that Yo’ash applied his heart on restoring the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.5: And he gathered the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Yahuḏah, and gather from all Yisra’ĕl silver to repair the House of your Elohim from year to year, and see that you hurry the matter.” But the Lĕwites did not hurry it.
24.6: And the meleḵ called Yahoyaḏa the chief, and said to him, “Why have you not required the Lĕwites to bring in from Yahuḏah and from Yerushalayim the levy of Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and of the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, for the Tent of the Witness?”
24.7: For the sons of Athalyahu, that wicked woman, had broken into the House of Elohim, and had also prepared all the qodesh vessels of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to the Ba’als.
24.8: So the meleḵ commanded and they made a chest, and put it outside at the gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
24.9: and made it known in Yahuḏah and in Yerushalayim to bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the levy that Mosheh the servant of Elohim had imposed on Yisra’ĕl in the wilderness.
24.10: And all the rulers and all the people rejoiced, and they brought in and put them into the chest to completion.
24.11: And it came to be, at that time, when the chest was brought to the meleḵ’s official by the hand of the Lĕwites, and when they saw that there was much silver, that the meleḵ’s scribe and the kohĕn ha’gadol’s officer came and emptied the chest, and took it and returned it to its place. So they did day by day, and gathered a large amount of silver.
24.12: And the meleḵ and Yahoyaḏa gave it to those who did the work of the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they hired stonemasons and carpenters to restore the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and also those who worked in iron and bronze to repair the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.13: And the workmen labored, and the work of restoration progressed in their hands, and they established the House of Elohim to its proper form and strengthened it.
24.14: And when they had finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the meleḵ and Yahoyaḏa, and they made utensils from it for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, utensils for serving and offering, ladles and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 continually all the days of Yahoyaḏa.
24.15: And Yahoyaḏa was old and satisfied with days, and died, one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
24.16: And they buried him in the City of Dawiḏ among the melaḵim, for he had done good in Yisra’ĕl, both toward Elohim and His house.
24.17: And after the death of Yahoyaḏa the rulers of Yahuḏah came and bowed themselves to the meleḵ. And the meleḵ listened to them,
24.18: and they forsook the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers, and served the Ashĕrim and the idols. And wrath came upon Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim because of their trespass.
24.19: And He sent neḇi’im to them, to bring them back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they witnessed against them, but they did not listen.
24.20: Then the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon Zeḵaryah son of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn, who stood above the people, and said to them, “Thus said Elohim, ‘Why are you transgressing the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and do not prosper? Because you have forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He has forsaken you.’ ”
24.21: And they conspired against him, and at the command of the meleḵ they stoned him with stones in the courtyard of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.22: Thus Yo’ash the meleḵ did not remember the kindness which Yahoyaḏa his father had done to him, and slew his son. And as he died, he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sees, and repays!”
24.23: And it came to be, at the turn of the year, that the army of Aram came up against him. And they came into Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, and destroyed all the rulers of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoil to the meleḵ of Darmeseq.
24.24: For the army of Aram came with few men, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave a very great army into their hand, because they had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Yo’ash.
24.25: And when they had withdrawn from him - for they left him very sick - his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn, and slew him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the City of Dawiḏ, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the melaḵim.
24.26: And these are the ones who conspired against him: Zaḇaḏ the son of Shim’ath the Ammonitess, and Yahozaḇaḏ the son of Shimrith the Mo’aḇitess.
24.27: As to his sons, and the many words about him, and the rebuilding of the House of Elohim, see, they are written in the commentary of the book of the melaḵim. And Amatsyahu his son reigned in his place.

25.1: Amatsyahu was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And the name of his mother was Yaho’addan of Yerushalayim.
25.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but not with a perfect heart.
25.3: And it came to be, upon his strong control of the reign, that he slew his servants who had smitten his father the meleḵ.
25.4: But he did not put their children to death, but did as it is written in the Torah in the Book of Mosheh, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded, saying, “Fathers are not put to death for their children, and children are not put to death for their fathers, but each one has to die for his own sin.”
25.5: And Amatsyahu gathered Yahuḏah and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, according to the fathers’ houses, for all Yahuḏah and Binyamin. And he registered them from twenty years old and above, and found them to be three hundred thousand choice men going out to the army, handling spear and shield.
25.6: And he hired one hundred thousand mighty brave ones from Yisra’ĕl for one hundred kiḵars of silver.
25.7: But a man of Elohim came to him, saying, “O meleḵ, do not let the army of Yisra’ĕl go with you, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is not with Yisra’ĕl, with all the children of Ephrayim.
25.8: “But if you are going, do it! Be strong in battle, or Elohim would make you fall before the enemy, for Elohim has power to help and to overthrow.”
25.9: And Amatsyahu said to the man of Elohim, “But what do we do about the hundred kiḵars which I have given to the army of Yisra’ĕl?” And the man of Elohim answered, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has more to give you than this.”
25.10: So Amatsyahu dismissed the army that had come to him from Ephrayim, to go back home. And they were greatly enraged against Yahuḏah, and they returned home in a rage.
25.11: And Amatsyahu strengthened himself, and led his people, and went to the Valley of Salt and smote ten thousand of the sons of Sĕ’ir.
25.12: And the sons of Yahuḏah took captive another ten thousand alive, and they brought them to the top of the rock, and threw them down from the top of the rock, and all of them were dashed to pieces.
25.13: And the soldiers of the army which Amatsyahu had sent back from going with him to battle, they raided the cities of Yahuḏah from Shomeron to Bĕyth Ḥoron, and smote three thousand in them, and took much spoil.
25.14: And it came to be, after Amatsyahu came from smiting the Eḏomites, that he brought the mighty ones of the people of Sĕ’ir, and stood them up to be his mighty ones, and bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
25.15: Therefore the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Amatsyahu, and He sent him a naḇi who said to him, “Why have you sought the mighty ones of the people, which did not deliver their own people from your hand?”
25.16: And it came to be, as he talked with him, that the meleḵ said to him, “Have we appointed you counsellor to the meleḵ? Stop! Why should they smite you?” Then the naḇi stopped and said, “I know that Elohim has counselled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.”
25.17: And Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah took counsel and sent to Yo’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz, son of Yahu, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “Come, let us look each other in the face!”
25.18: And Yo’ash meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl sent to Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying, “The thistle that was in Leḇanon sent to the cedar that was in Leḇanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ And a wild beast that was in Leḇanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
25.19: “You have said, ‘See, I have smitten Eḏom,’ and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay at home, why should you stir up yourself to evil, that you should fall - you and Yahuḏah with you?”
25.20: But Amatsyahu did not listen, for it came from Elohim, in order to give them into the hand of their enemies, because they had sought the mighty ones of Eḏom.
25.21: So Yo’ash meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl went out. And he and Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah faced one another at Bĕyth Shemesh, which belongs to Yahuḏah.
25.22: And Yahuḏah was smitten before Yisra’ĕl, and they each fled to his tent.
25.23: And Yo’ash the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl caught Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, son of Yo’ash, son of Yaho’aḥaz, at Bĕyth Shemesh, and brought him to Yerushalayim, and broke down the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Ephrayim to the Corner Gate, four hundred ammah,
25.24: and took all the gold and the silver, and all the utensils that were found in the House of Elohim with Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and the treasures of the meleḵ’s house, and hostages, and returned to Shomeron.
25.25: And Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yo’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
25.26: And the rest of the acts of Amatsyahu, from the first to the last, see, are they not written in the book of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah and Yisra’ĕl?
25.27: And from the time that Amatsyahu turned away from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Laḵish. And they sent after him to Laḵish and killed him there,
25.28: and they brought him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Yahuḏah.

26.1: And all people of Yahuḏah took Uzziyahu, who was sixteen years old, and appointed him to reign instead of his father Amatsyahu.
26.2: He built Ĕyloth and restored it to Yahuḏah, after the meleḵ slept with his fathers.
26.3: Uzziyahu was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḵolyah of Yerushalayim.
26.4: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father Amatsyahu did.
26.5: And he sought Elohim in the days of Zeḵaryahu, who had understanding in the visions of Elohim. And while he sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Elohim made him prosper.
26.6: And he went out and fought against the Pelishtites, and broke down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Yaḇneh, and the wall of Ashdoḏ, and built cities around Ashdoḏ and among the Pelishtites.
26.7: And Elohim helped him against the Pelishtites, and against the Araḇians who lived in Gur Ba’al, and the Me’unites.
26.8: And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziyahu. And his name spread as far as the entrance of Mitsrayim, for he strengthened himself greatly.
26.9: And Uzziyahu built towers in Yerushalayim at the Corner Gate, and at the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress, and strengthened them.
26.10: And he built towers in the wilderness, and dug many wells, for he had much livestock, both in the low country and in the plain, farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Karmel, for he loved the soil.
26.11: And Uzziyahu had an army of fighting men who went out to battle by divisions, according to the number on their roll as prepared by Ye’i’ĕl the scribe and Ma’asĕyahu the officer, under the hand of Ḥananyahu, one of the meleḵ’s commanders.
26.12: The total number of the clan chiefs of the mighty brave ones was two thousand six hundred.
26.13: And under their hand was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred that fought with mighty power, to help the meleḵ against the enemy.
26.14: And Uzziyahu prepared for them, for the entire army, shields, and spears, and helmets, and body armor, and bows, and sling stones.
26.15: And he made machines in Yerushalayim, devised by skilled men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. And his name spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped till he became strong.
26.16: But when he became strong his heart was lifted up, to his destruction, for he trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim by entering the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to burn incense on the altar of incense.
26.17: And Azaryahu the kohĕn went in after him, and with him were eighty kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who were brave men.
26.18: And they stood up against Meleḵ Uzziyahu, and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziyahu, to burn incense to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but for the kohenim, the sons of Aharon, who are qodesh to burn incense. Get out of the Miqdash, for you have trespassed, and there is no esteem to you from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.”
26.19: And Uzziyahu was wroth. And he had a censer in his hand to burn incense. And while he was wroth with the kohenim, leprosy broke out on his forehead, before the kohenim in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, beside the incense altar.
26.20: And Azaryahu the chief kohĕn and all the kohenim looked at him, and saw that he was leprous on his forehead. And they hurried him from there. And he also hurried to get out, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had struck him.
26.21: And Meleḵ Uzziyahu was a leper until the day of his death, and dwelt in a separate house, because he was a leper, for he was cut off from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Yotham his son was over the meleḵ’s house, ruling the people of the land.
26.22: And the rest of the acts of Uzziyahu, from the first to the last, the naḇi Yeshayahu the son of Amots wrote.
26.23: So Uzziyahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the melaḵim, for they said, “He is a leper.” And Yotham his son reigned in his place.

27.1: Yotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yerushah the daughter of Tsaḏoq.
27.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father Uzziyahu had done. Only, he did not come into the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the people continued to act corruptly.
27.3: He built the Upper Gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and he built much on the wall of Ophel.
27.4: And he built cities in the hill country of Yahuḏah, and in the forests he built palaces and towers.
27.5: And he fought with the meleḵ of the Ammonites and prevailed over them. And the children of Ammon gave him in that year one hundred kiḵars of silver, and ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. This is what the children of Ammon paid him, also in the second and third years.
27.6: And Yotham strengthened himself, for he prepared his ways before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
27.7: And the rest of the acts of Yotham, and all his battles and his ways, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.
27.8: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim.
27.9: So Yotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Dawiḏ. And his son Aḥaz reigned in his place.

28.1: Aḥaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as his father Dawiḏ had done,
28.2: and walked in the ways of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl, and made molded images for the Ba’als.
28.3: And he himself burned incense in the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, and burned his children in the fire, according to the abominations of the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ĕl,
28.4: and slaughtered and burned incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.
28.5: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim gave him into the hand of the meleḵ of Aram, and they smote him, and took many of them away as captives, and brought them to Dammeseq. And he was also given into the hand of the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, who smote him with a great smiting.
28.6: And Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu slew one hundred and twenty thousand in Yahuḏah in one day, all brave men, because they had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.
28.7: And Ziḵri, a mighty man of Ephrayim, slew Ma’asĕyahu son of the meleḵ, and Azriqam the officer over the house, and Elqanah who was second to the meleḵ.
28.8: And the children of Yisra’ĕl took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters. And they also seized from them much spoil, and they brought the spoil to Shomeron.
28.9: But a naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was there, whose name was Oḏĕḏ. And he went out before the army that came to Shomeron, and said to them, “See, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers was displeased with Yahuḏah, He has given them into your hand, and you have slain them in a rage that reaches up to the shamayim.
28.10: “And now you are planning to make the children of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim your male and female slaves, but are you not also guilty before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim?
28.11: “Now therefore, listen to me, and return the captives whom you have taken captive from your brothers, for the heat of the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon you.”
28.12: And some of the heads of the children of Ephrayim: Azaryahu son of Yahoḥanan, Bereḵyahu son of Meshillĕmoth, and Yeḥizqiyahu son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Ḥaḏlai, stood up against those who came from the army,
28.13: and said to them, “Do not bring the captives here, to bring on us guilt before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Are you planning to add to our sins and to our guilt? For our guilt is great, and burning is the wrath on Yisra’ĕl.”
28.14: And the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the leaders and all the assembly.
28.15: And the men who were designated by name rose up and took the captives, and from the spoil they clothed all the naked among them, dressed them and gave them sandals, and gave them food and drink, and anointed them, and let all the weak ones ride on donkeys, and brought them to their brothers at Yeriḥo, the city of palm trees, then returned to Shomeron.
28.16: At that time Meleḵ Aḥaz sent to the melaḵim of Ashshur to help him.
28.17: For the Eḏomites had come again, and smote Yahuḏah, and took away captives.
28.18: And the Pelishtites invaded the cities of the low country and of the South of Yahuḏah, and captured Bĕyth Shemesh, and Ayalon, and Geḏĕroth, and Soḵo with its villages, and Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages, and dwelt there.
28.19: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had brought Yahuḏah low because of Aḥaz meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, for he brought about a lack of restraint in Yahuḏah and trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
28.20: And Tiḡlath-Pileser the meleḵ of Ashshur came against him and distressed him, and did not help him,
28.21: though Aḥaz had taken some of the treasures from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the house of the meleḵ, and from the leaders, and he gave it to the meleḵ of Ashshur, but he did not help him.
28.22: And in the time of his distress Meleḵ Aḥaz trespassed even more against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - this Meleḵ Aḥaz -
28.23: and he slaughtered to the mighty ones of Dammeseq, those smiting him, saying, “Because the mighty ones of the melaḵim of Aram help them, I offer to them and they help me.” But they were to cause him and all Yisra’ĕl to stumble.
28.24: And Aḥaz gathered the utensils of the House of Elohim, and cut in pieces the utensils of the House of Elohim, and shut the doors of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and made for himself altars in every corner of Yerushalayim.
28.25: And in every city, even the cities of Yahuḏah, he made high places to burn incense to other mighty ones, and provoked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of his fathers.
28.26: And the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah and Yisra’ĕl.
28.27: So Aḥaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Yerushalayim, but they did not bring him into the tombs of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl. And Ḥizqiyahu his son reigned in his place.

29.1: Ḥizqiyahu began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Aḇiyah the daughter of Zeḵaryahu.
29.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father Dawiḏ did.
29.3: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and repaired them,
29.4: and brought in the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and gathered them in the open place to the east.
29.5: And he said to them, “Listen to me, O Lĕwites! Now qadosh yourselves, qadosh the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers, and remove the uncleanness from the qodesh place.
29.6: “For our fathers have trespassed and have done evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, and have forsaken Him, and have turned their faces away from the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and have given their backs.
29.7: “And they have shut the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and they have not burned incense or offered burnt offerings in the qodesh place to the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
29.8: “Therefore the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell upon Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, and He has given them up for a trembling, for an astonishment, and for a hissing, as you see with your eyes.
29.9: “And see, because of this our fathers have fallen by the sword. And our sons, and our daughters, and our wives are in captivity for this.
29.10: “Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, so that the heat of His wrath turns away from us.
29.11: “My sons, do not be slack, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen you to stand before Him, to serve Him, and to be attendants for Him and burn incense.”
29.12: And the Lĕwites rose up: Maḥath son of Amasai and Yo’ĕl son of Azaryahu, of the sons of the Qehathites; and of the sons of Merari, Qish son of Aḇdi and Azaryahu son of Yehallel’ĕl; and of the Gĕreshonites, Yo’aḥ son of Zimmah and Ĕḏen son of Yo’aḥ;
29.13: and of the sons of Elitsaphan, Shimri and Ye’i’ĕl; and of the sons of Asaph, Zeḵaryahu and Mattanyahu;
29.14: and of the sons of Hĕman, Yeḥi’ĕl and Shim’i and of the sons of Yeḏuthun, Shemayah and Uzzi’ĕl.
29.15: And they gathered their brothers, and qadosh themselves, and went according to the command of the meleḵ, at the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to cleanse the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.16: And the kohenim came into the inner part of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness they found in the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to the courtyard of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Then the Lĕwites received it to take it outside to the wadi Qiḏron.
29.17: And they began to qadosh on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they qadosh the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they had finished.
29.18: Then they came in to Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu and said, “We have cleansed all the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the altar of burnt offerings with all its utensils, and the table of the showbread with all its utensils.
29.19: “And all the utensils which Meleḵ Aḥaz in his reign had pushed aside, when he trespassed, we have prepared and qadosh. And see, they are before the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
29.20: And Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu rose up early, and gathered the heads of the city, and went up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.21: And they brought seven bulls, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the reign, for the Miqdash, and for Yahuḏah. And he said to the kohenim, the sons of Aharon, to offer them on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.22: So they slaughtered the bulls, and the kohenim received the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. And they slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood on the altar. And they slaughtered the lambs and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
29.23: And they brought out the male goats of the sin offering before the meleḵ and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them,
29.24: and the kohenim slaughtered them, and with their blood made a sin offering on the altar, to make an atonement for all Yisra’ĕl, for the meleḵ said that the burnt offering and the sin offering is for all Yisra’ĕl.
29.25: And he appointed the Lĕwites in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with cymbals, with harps, and with lyres, according to the command of Dawiḏ, and of Gaḏ, seer of the meleḵ, and of Nathan the naḇi, for the command was by the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, by the hand of His neḇi’im.
29.26: And the Lĕwites stood with the instruments of Dawiḏ, and the kohenim with the trumpets.
29.27: And Ḥizqiyahu gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the singing unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 began, with the trumpets and with the instruments of Dawiḏ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
29.28: And all the assembly were bowing, and the singers singing, and the trumpeters blowing - all this until the burnt offering was completed.
29.29: And at the completion of the offering, the meleḵ and all who were present with him bowed and worshipped.
29.30: And Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu and the rulers ordered the Lĕwites to sing praise to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with the words of Dawiḏ and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.
29.31: And Ḥizqiyahu responded and said, “Now that you have ordained yourselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, come near, and bring slaughterings and thank offerings into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And the assembly brought in slaughterings and thank offerings, and all those whose hearts were so moved brought burnt offerings.
29.32: And the number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs - all these for a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
29.33: And the qodesh gifts were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.
29.34: Only, the kohenim were too few, and were unable to skin all the burnt offerings, so their brothers the Lĕwites helped them until the work was completed and until the other kohenim had qadosh themselves, for the Lĕwites were more upright of heart to qadosh themselves, than the kohenim.
29.35: And there were also many burnt offerings, with the fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for every burnt offering. Thus the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was reestablished.
29.36: And Ḥizqiyahu and all the people rejoiced that Elohim had prepared the people, because the matter came about so suddenly.

3.1: And Shelomoh began to build the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim on Mount Moriyah, where He appeared to his father Dawiḏ, at the place that Dawiḏ had prepared on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
3.2: And he began to build on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
3.3: And these are the foundations which Shelomoh laid for building the House of Elohim: The length by ammah according to the former measure were sixty ammah, and the width twenty ammah.
3.4: And the porch that was in front was twenty ammah long according to the breadth of the House, and the height was one hundred and twenty. And he overlaid the inside with clean gold.
3.5: And the great House he paneled with cypress which he overlaid with fine gold, and he carved palm trees and chainwork on it.
3.6: And he covered the House with precious stones for comeliness, and the gold was gold from Parwayim.
3.7: And he overlaid the House, the beams, the doorposts, and its walls, and its doors with gold, and carved keruḇim on the walls.
3.8: And he made the House of the Most Qodesh. Its length was according to the width of the House, twenty ammah, and its width twenty ammah. And he overlaid it with fine gold, six hundred kiḵars.
3.9: And the weight of the nails was fifty sheqels of gold. And he overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
