3.10: In the Most Qodesh House he made two keruḇim of sculptured work, and overlaid them with gold.
3.11: And the wings of the keruḇim: their length was twenty ammah, one wing was five ammah, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing was five ammah, touching the wing of the other keruḇ,
3.12: and the wing of the other keruḇ was five ammah, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing also was five ammah, touching the wing of the other keruḇ.
3.13: The wings of these keruḇim spread out twenty ammah, and they stood on their feet, and they faced inward.
3.14: And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and worked keruḇim on it.
3.15: And at the front of the House he made two columns thirty-five ammah high, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five ammah.
3.16: And he made wreaths of chainwork, as in the Speaking Place, and put them on top of the columns. And he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the wreaths of chainwork.
3.17: And he put up the columns before the Hĕyḵal, one on the right and the other on the left, and called the name of the one on the right Yaḵin, and the name of the one on the left Bo’az.

30.1: And Ḥizqiyahu sent to all Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah, and he also wrote letters to Ephrayim and Menashsheh, to come to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim, to perform the Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
30.2: But the meleḵ and his leaders and all the assembly in Yerushalayim had taken counsel to perform the Pesaḥ in the second month.
30.3: For they were unable to perform it at its time, because not enough kohenim had qadosh themselves, and the people had not gathered at Yerushalayim.
30.4: And the matter was right in the eyes of the meleḵ and in the eyes of all the assembly.
30.5: And they settled the matter, to send a call to all Yisra’ĕl, from Be’ĕrsheḇa to Dan, to come to perform a Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl at Yerushalayim, since they had not done it for a long time, as it is written.
30.6: And the runners went to all Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah with the letters from the meleḵ and his leaders, and spoke according to the command of the meleḵ, “Children of Yisra’ĕl, turn back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yisra’ĕl, so that He returns to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the melaḵim of Ashshur.
30.7: “And do not be like your fathers and like your brothers, who trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers, so that He gave them up to ruin, as you see.
30.8: “Now do not stiffen your neck, like your fathers, stretch forth the hand to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and come to His Miqdash, which He has qadosh forever, and serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, so that His burning wrath turns away from you.
30.9: “For if you turn back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, your brothers and your children shall be shown compassion by their captors, even to return to this land. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shows favor and compassion, and does not turn His face from you if you turn back to Him.”
30.10: And the runners passed from city to city throughout the land of Ephrayim and Menashsheh, as far as Zeḇulun. But they were laughing at them and mocking them.
30.11: Some from Ashĕr and Menashsheh and from Zeḇulun, however, humbled themselves and came to Yerushalayim.
30.12: Also the hand of Elohim was on Yahuḏah to give them one heart to do the command of the meleḵ and the rulers, at the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
30.13: And many people, a very great assembly, gathered at Yerushalayim to perform the Festival of Matstsoth in the second month.
30.14: And they rose up and removed the altars that were in Yerushalayim, and they removed all the incense altars and threw them into the wadi Qiḏron.
30.15: Then they slaughtered the Pesaḥ on the fourteenth day of the second month. And the kohenim and the Lĕwites were ashamed, and qadosh themselves, and brought the burnt offerings to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
30.16: And they stood in their place according to their right-ruling. According to the Torah of Mosheh, the man of Elohim, the kohenim sprinkled the blood from the hand of the Lĕwites.
30.17: For many in the assembly had not qadosh themselves. Therefore the Lĕwites were over the slaughter of the Pesaḥ for everyone who was not clean, to qadosh them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
30.18: For many of the people, many from Ephrayim and Menashsheh, Yissasḵar and Zeḇulun, had not been cleansed, yet they ate the Pesaḥ contrary to what was written. But Ḥizqiyahu prayed for them, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is good, provide atonement for everyone
30.19: who has prepared his heart to seek Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of his fathers, though he is not cleansed according to the cleansing of the qodesh place.”
30.20: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 listened to Ḥizqiyahu and healed the people.
30.21: And the children of Yisra’ĕl who were in Yerushalayim performed the Festival of Matstsoth seven days with great joy. And the Lĕwites and the kohenim praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 day by day, with instruments of praise before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
30.22: And Ḥizqiyahu spoke to the heart of all the Lĕwites, those having good understanding concerning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So they ate what was appointed, seven days, slaughtering peace offerings and making confession to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.
30.23: And all the assembly took counsel to perform another seven days, and they performed it another seven days with joy.
30.24: For Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah presented to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the rulers presented to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. And a great number of kohenim qadosh themselves.
30.25: And all the assembly of Yahuḏah rejoiced, and the kohenim and Lĕwites, and all the assembly who had come from Yisra’ĕl, and the sojourners who came from the land of Yisra’ĕl, and those who dwelt in Yahuḏah.
30.26: And there came to be great joy in Yerushalayim, for since the days of Shelomoh son of Dawiḏ, the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, the like of this had not been in Yerushalayim.
30.27: And the kohenim, the Lĕwites, rose and baraḵ the people, and their voice was heard. And their prayer came up to His qodesh dwelling place, to the shamayim.

31.1: And at the completion of all this, all Yisra’ĕl who were present went out to the cities of Yahuḏah and broke down the pillars, and cut down the Ashĕrim, and tore down the high places and the altars, from all Yahuḏah, and Binyamin, and in Ephrayim and Menashsheh, even to completion. Then all the children of Yisra’ĕl returned to their own cities, each to his possession.
31.2: And Ḥizqiyahu appointed the divisions of the kohenim and of the Lĕwites according to their divisions, each according to his service of the kohenim and Lĕwites for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to serve and to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of the camp of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.3: And the meleḵ allotted from his possessions for the burnt offerings, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Shabbathoth and for the New Moons and for the Appointed Times, as it is written in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.4: And he said to the people, those who dwelt in Yerushalayim, to give the portion for the kohenim and the Lĕwites, so that they are strengthened in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
31.5: And as the word spread, the children of Yisra’ĕl brought large quantities of the first-fruits of grain and wine, and oil and honey, and of all the increase of the field. And they brought in the tithe of all, a large amount.
31.6: And the children of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah, those who dwelt in the cities of Yahuḏah, brought the tithe of cattle and sheep. Even the tithe of qodesh gifts which were qadosh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim were brought in, and they gave heaps, heaps.
31.7: In the third month they began to pile up the heaps, and they finished in the seventh month.
31.8: And Ḥizqiyahu and the leaders came and saw the heaps, and they baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His people Yisra’ĕl.
31.9: And Ḥizqiyahu asked the kohenim and the Lĕwites about the heaps.
31.10: And Azaryahu the chief kohĕn, from the house of Tsaḏoq, answered him and said, “Since they began to bring the offerings into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, we have had enough to eat and have plenty left, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has baraḵ His people. And this great amount is left over.”
31.11: And Ḥizqiyahu ordered them to prepare rooms in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and they prepared them.
31.12: Then they brought in the contribution, and the tithes, and the qodesh gifts, trustworthily. And Konanyahu the Lĕwite was leader over them, and Shim’i his brother was the next.
31.13: And Yeḥi’ĕl, and Azazyahu, and Naḥath, and Asah’ĕl, and Yerimoth, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Eli’ĕl, and Yismaḵyahu, and Maḥath, and Benayahu were overseers under the hand of Konanyahu and Shim’i his brother, by order of Ḥizqiyahu the meleḵ and Azaryahu the ruler of the House of Elohim.
31.14: And Qorĕ son of Yimnah the Lĕwite, the keeper of the East Gate, was over the voluntary offerings to Elohim, to distribute the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the most qodesh gifts.
31.15: And under his hand were Ĕḏen, and Minyamin, and Yĕshua, and Shemayahu, Amaryahu, and Sheḵanyahu, in the cities of the kohenim, to distribute trustworthily to their brothers by divisions, to the great as well as the small.
31.16: Besides those males from three years old and up who were written in the genealogy, they distributed to everyone who entered the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his daily portion for the work of his service, by his division,
31.17: and to the kohenim who were written in the genealogy according to their father’s house, and to the Lĕwites from twenty years old upward, by their duties in their divisions,
31.18: and to all listed in the genealogy, their little ones and their wives, their sons and daughters, all the company of them. For in their trustworthiness they qadosh themselves in qodeshah.
31.19: And for the sons of Aharon the kohenim, who were in the fields of the open land of their cities, in each and every city, there were men who were called by name to distribute portions to all the males among the kohenim and to all who were listed by genealogies among the Lĕwites.
31.20: And Ḥizqiyahu did this in all Yahuḏah, and he did what was good and what was right and what was true before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
31.21: And in every work that he began in the service of the House of Elohim, in the Torah and in the Command, to seek his Elohim, with all his heart, he did and prospered.

32.1: After these matters and this trustworthiness, Sanḥĕriḇ meleḵ of Ashshur came. And he entered Yahuḏah and encamped against the cities of defense, and said to break them open to himself.
32.2: And Ḥizqiyahu saw that Sanḥĕriḇ had come, and his face turned to fight against Yerushalayim,
32.3: and he took counsel with his rulers and mighty men to stop the water from the springs which were outside the city. And they helped him.
32.4: And many people were gathered, and they stopped all the springs and the stream that ran through the land, saying, “Why should the melaḵim of Ashshur come and find much water?”
32.5: And he strengthened himself, and built up all the wall that was broken, and raised it up to the towers, and outside of it another wall, and strengthened Millo, the City of Dawiḏ, and made large numbers of weapons and shields.
32.6: And he appointed battle officers over the people, and gathered them to him in the open space at the city gate, and spoke to their heart, saying,
32.7: “Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid nor be cast down before the meleḵ of Ashshur, nor before all the army that is with him. For with us there are more than with him.
32.8: “With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people leaned on the words of Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah.
32.9: After this Sanḥĕriḇ the meleḵ of Ashshur sent his servants to Yerushalayim - but he himself, and all his power with him against Laḵish - to Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and to all Yahuḏah who were in Yerushalayim, saying,
32.10: “Thus said Sanḥĕriḇ the meleḵ of Ashshur, ‘On what are you trusting, that you remain in Yerushalayim under siege?
32.11: ‘Is Ḥizqiyahu not persuading you to give yourselves over to die by scarcity of food and by thirst, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim shall deliver us from the hand of the meleḵ of Ashshur”?
32.12: ‘Has not Ḥizqiyahu himself taken away His high places and His altars, and ordered Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, saying, “Bow yourselves before one altar and burn incense on it?”
32.13: ‘Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the mighty ones of the nations of those lands in any way able to deliver their lands out of my hand?
32.14: ‘Who was there among all the mighty ones of those nations that my fathers put under the ban that could deliver his people from my hand, that your Elohim should be able to deliver you from my hand?
32.15: ‘And now, do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive you or persuade you like this, and do not believe him; for no mighty one of any nation or reign was able to deliver his people from my hand or the hand of my fathers - much less your Elohim, to deliver you from my hand!’ ”
32.16: And his servants spoke even more against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim and against His servant Ḥizqiyahu.
32.17: And he wrote letters to reproach 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and to speak against Him, saying, “As the mighty ones of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the Elohim of Ḥizqiyahu shall not deliver His people from my hand.”
32.18: Then they called out with a loud voice in the language of Yahuḏah to the people of Yerushalayim who were on the wall, to frighten them and to trouble them, in order to capture the city.
32.19: And they spoke against the Elohim of Yerushalayim, as against the mighty ones of the people of the earth, the work of men’s hands.
32.20: And Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu and the naḇi Yeshayahu, son of Amots, prayed about this, and cried out to the shamayim.
32.21: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent a messenger who cut down every mighty brave one, both the leader and the commander in the camp of the meleḵ of Ashshur, and he returned shamefaced to his own land, and went into the house of his mighty one, and there some of his own offspring caused him to fall by the sword.
32.22: Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Ḥizqiyahu and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim from the hand of Sanḥĕriḇ the meleḵ of Ashshur, and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side.
32.23: And many brought gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim, and presents to Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and he was exalted in the eyes of all nations thereafter.
32.24: In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick and near death, and he prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And He spoke to him and appointed a sign for him.
32.25: However, Ḥizqiyahu did not repay according to the good done to him, for his heart was lifted up, therefore wrath came upon him and upon Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
32.26: Then Ḥizqiyahu humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so that the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did not come upon them in the days of Ḥizqiyahu.
32.27: And Ḥizqiyahu had much riches and esteem. And he made himself treasuries for silver, and for gold, and for precious stones, and for spices, and for shields, and for all desirable utensils;
32.28: and storehouses for the harvest of grain, and wine, and oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and folds for flocks.
32.29: And he made cities for himself, and possessions of great numbers of flocks and herds, for Elohim gave him much property.
32.30: And Ḥizqiyahu himself had stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Giḥon, and directed them to the west side of the City of Dawiḏ. And Ḥizqiyahu prospered in all his work.
32.31: However with the envoys of the princes of Baḇel, whom they sent to ask him about the wonder that was done in the land, Elohim left him, in order to try him, to know all that was in his heart.
32.32: And the rest of the acts of Ḥizqiyahu, and his kindness, see, they are written in the vision of Yeshayahu the naḇi, son of Amots, in the book of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah and Yisra’ĕl.
32.33: So Ḥizqiyahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the upper tombs of the sons of Dawiḏ. And all Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim esteemed him at his death. And Menashsheh his son reigned in his place.

33.1: Menashsheh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yerushalayim.
33.2: But he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to the abominations of the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
33.3: For again he rebuilt the high places which Ḥizqiyahu his father had broken down, and raised up altars for the Ba’alim, and made Ashĕroth, and bowed himself to all the host of the heavens and served them.
33.4: And he built altars in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said, “In Yerushalayim is My Name, forever.”
33.5: And he built altars for all the host of the heavens in the two courtyards of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
33.6: And he made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, and practiced magic, and used divination and witchcraft, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to provoke Him.
33.7: And he placed a carved image of the idol which he had made, in the House of Elohim, of which Elohim had said to Dawiḏ and to Shelomoh his son, “In this house and in Yerushalayim, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, I put My Name forever,
33.8: and no more shall I remove the foot of Yisra’ĕl from the land which I have appointed for your fathers - only if they guard to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the Torah and the Laws and the Right-Rulings by the hand of Mosheh.”
33.9: Thus Menashsheh led Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim astray, to do more evil than the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had destroyed before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
33.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Menashsheh and to his people, but they did not listen.
33.11: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brought upon them the commanders of the army of the meleḵ of Ashshur, who captured Menashsheh with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles, and made him go to Baḇel.
33.12: And when he was in distress, he sought the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, and humbled himself greatly before the Elohim of his fathers,
33.13: and prayed to Him. And He was moved by his entreaty and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Yerushalayim into his malḵuth. And Menashsheh knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was Elohim.
33.14: And after this he built a wall outside the City of Dawiḏ on the west of Giḥon, in the wadi, and as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate, and it went round Ophel, and he made it exceedingly high. And he put army commanders in all the walled cities of Yahuḏah.
33.15: And he removed the foreign mighty ones and the idol from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in Yerushalayim, and he threw them out of the city.
33.16: And he built the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and brought peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and ordered Yahuḏah to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
33.17: But the people were still offering on the high places, though only to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim.
33.18: And the rest of the acts of Menashsheh, his prayer to his Elohim, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the Name 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
33.19: And his prayer, and his entreaty, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places where he built high places and stood up the Ashĕrim and the carved images, before he was humbled, see, they are written among the words of the seers.
33.20: So Menashsheh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. And his son Amon reigned in his place.
33.21: Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Yerushalayim.
33.22: But he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as his father Menashsheh had done. And Amon offered to all the carved images which his father Menashsheh had made, and served them.
33.23: And he did not humble himself before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as his father Menashsheh had humbled himself, for Amon trespassed more and more.
33.24: And his servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house.
33.25: But the people of the land smote all those who had conspired against Meleḵ Amon, and the people of the land appointed his son Yoshiyahu to reign in his place.

34.1: Yoshiyahu was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Yerushalayim.
34.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and walked in the ways of his father Dawiḏ, and did not turn aside, right or left.
34.3: And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the Elohim of his father Dawiḏ. And in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim from the high places, and the Ashĕrim, and the carved images, and the molded images.
34.4: And they broke down the altars of the Ba’als in his presence, and the sun-pillars which were above them he cut down. And the Ashĕrim, and the carved images, and the molded images he destroyed, and ground them up and scattered it on the graves of those who had offered to them.
34.5: And he burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim,
34.6: and in the cities of Menashsheh, and Ephrayim, and Shim’on, as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around.
34.7: And he broke down the altars and the Ashĕrim, and ground the carved images into dust, and cut down all the sun-pillars throughout all the land of Yisra’ĕl, and returned to Yerushalayim.
34.8: And in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the House, he sent Shaphan son of Atsalyahu, and Ma’asĕyahu the head of the city, and Yo’aḥ son of Yo’aḥaz the recorder, to repair the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
34.9: And they went to Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn ha’gadol, and they gave the silver that was brought into the House of Elohim, which the Lĕwites who kept the doors had gathered from the hand of Menashsheh and Ephrayim, and from all the remnant of Yisra’ĕl, and from all Yahuḏah and Binyamin, and which they had brought back to Yerushalayim,
34.10: and they gave it in the hand of the workmen, those appointed over the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they gave it to the workmen who worked in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to repair and strengthen the House.
34.11: And they gave it to the craftsmen and to the builders, to buy hewn stone and timber for couplings and for beams for the houses which the melaḵim of Yahuḏah had destroyed.
34.12: And the men did the work trustworthily. And over them were appointed Yaḥath and Oḇaḏyahu the Lĕwites, of the sons of Merari, and Zeḵaryah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Qehathites, to oversee; and of the Lĕwites, all of whom were skilled in instruments of song,
34.13: and over the burden bearers, and overseers of all who did work in any kind of service. And of the Lĕwites were scribes, and officers, and gatekeepers.
34.14: And when they brought out the silver that was brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn found the Book of the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 given by Mosheh.
34.15: Then Ḥilqiyahu responded and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Torah in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And Ḥilqiyahu gave the Book to Shaphan.
34.16: And Shaphan brought the Book to the meleḵ, and brought the meleḵ word, saying, “All that has been given into the hand of your servants, they are doing.
34.17: “And they have poured out the silver that was found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and have given it into the hand of those appointed and the workmen.”
34.18: And Shaphan the scribe informed the meleḵ, saying, “Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn has given me a Book.” And Shaphan read it before the meleḵ.
34.19: And it came to be when the meleḵ heard the words of the Torah, that he tore his garments.
34.20: And the meleḵ commanded Ḥilqiyahu, Aḥiqam son of Shaphan, and Aḇdon son of Miḵah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asayah a servant of the meleḵ, saying,
34.21: “Go, inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for me, and for him who is left in Yisra’ĕl and in Yahuḏah, concerning the words of the Book that is found. For great is the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that is poured out on us, because our fathers have not guarded the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to do according to all that is written in this Book.”
34.22: Then Ḥilqiyahu and those of the meleḵ went to Ḥuldah the neḇiyah, the wife of Shallum son of Toqhath, son of Ḥasrah, keeper of the wardrobe, who was dwelling in Yerushalayim in the Second Quarter. And they spoke to her about this.
34.23: And she said to them, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Say to the man who sent you to Me,
34.24: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am bringing evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the Book which they have read before the meleḵ of Yahuḏah,
34.25: because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other mighty ones, to provoke Me with all the works of their hands. Therefore My wrath is poured out on this place, and is not quenched.’ ” ’
34.26: “And to the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, who sent you to inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, say this to him, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, whose words you have heard,
34.27: “Because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before Elohim when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me, and you tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
34.28: “See, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, so that your eyes would not see all the evil that I am bringing on this place and its inhabitants.” ’ ” So they brought back word to the meleḵ.
34.29: And the meleḵ sent and gathered all the elders of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
34.30: And the meleḵ went up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all the men of Yahuḏah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and all the people, both great and small. And he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant which had been found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
34.31: And the meleḵ stood in his place and made a covenant before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and to guard His Commands and His Witnesses and His Laws, with all his heart and all his being, to do the words of the Covenant that were written in this Book.
34.32: And he made stand all who were present in Yerushalayim and Binyamin. And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim did according to the Covenant of Elohim, the Elohim of their fathers.
34.33: And Yoshiyahu removed all the abominations from all the lands that belonged to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and made all who were present in Yisra’ĕl diligently serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim. All his days they did not turn away from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers.

35.1: And Yoshiyahu performed a Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Yerushalayim, and they slaughtered the Pesaḥ on the fourteenth day of the first month.
35.2: And he appointed the kohenim in their duties and strengthened them for the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
35.3: and said to the Lĕwites who were teaching all Yisra’ĕl, who were qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Put the qodesh ark in the House which Shelomoh son of Dawiḏ, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, built. It is no longer to be a burden on your shoulders. Now serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and His people Yisra’ĕl,
35.4: and prepare by the fathers’ houses, according to your divisions, by the writing of Dawiḏ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl and by the writing of Shelomoh his son.
35.5: “And stand in the qodesh place by the divisions of the fathers’ houses of your brothers the lay people, and the portion of the father’s house of the Lĕwites.
35.6: “And slaughter the Pesaḥ, and qadosh yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the hand of Mosheh.”
35.7: And Yoshiyahu gave the lay people lambs and young goats from the flock, all for Pesaḥ for everyone present, to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand cattle - these were from the meleḵ’s possessions.
35.8: And his leaders contributed a voluntary offering to the people, to the kohenim, and to the Lĕwites. Ḥilqiyahu, and Zeḵaryahu, and Yeḥi’ĕl, leaders of the House of Elohim, gave to the kohenim for the Pesaḥ two thousand six hundred, and three hundred cattle;
35.9: and Konanyahu, his brothers Shemayahu and Nethan’ĕl, and Ḥashaḇyahu and Ye’i’ĕl and Yozaḇaḏ, chiefs of the Lĕwites, gave to the Lĕwites for Pesaḥ offerings five thousand, and five hundred cattle.
35.10: And the service was prepared, and the kohenim stood in their places, and the Lĕwites in their divisions, according to the command of the meleḵ,
35.11: and they slaughtered the Pesaḥ. And the kohenim sprinkled out of their hands, while the Lĕwites were skinning.
35.12: And they removed the burnt offerings, to give them to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of the lay people, to bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as it is written in the Book of Mosheh, and the same with the cattle.
35.13: So they roasted the Pesaḥ with fire according to the Right-Ruling, and they boiled the qodesh offerings in pots, and in cauldrons, and in bowls, and brought them speedily to all the lay people.
35.14: And afterward they prepared for themselves and for the kohenim, because the kohenim, the sons of Aharon, were offering burnt offerings and fat until night. So the Lĕwites prepared for themselves and for the kohenim, the sons of Aharon.
35.15: And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their places, according to the command of Dawiḏ, and Asaph, and Hĕman, and Yeḏuthun the seer of the meleḵ. And the gatekeepers at each gate did not have to leave their position, because their brothers the Lĕwites prepared for them.
35.16: And all the service of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was prepared that day, to perform the Pesaḥ and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to the command of Meleḵ Yoshiyahu.
35.17: And the children of Yisra’ĕl who were present performed the Pesaḥ at that time, and the Festival of Matstsoth for seven days.
35.18: There had not been a Pesaḥ performed in Yisra’ĕl like it since the days of Shemu’ĕl the naḇi. And none of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl had performed such a Pesaḥ as Yoshiyahu performed, with the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and all Yahuḏah and Yisra’ĕl who were present, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
35.19: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Yoshiyahu this Pesaḥ was performed.
35.20: After all this, when Yoshiyahu had prepared the House, Neḵo meleḵ of Mitsrayim came up to fight against Karkemish by Perath. And Yoshiyahu went out against him.
35.21: And he sent messengers to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, meleḵ of Yahuḏah? I am not coming against you this day, but against the house with which I am fighting, for Elohim commanded me to make haste. Leave Elohim alone, who is with me, lest He destroy you.”
35.22: However, Yoshiyahu would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself to fight against him, and did not listen to the words of Neḵo from the mouth of Elohim, and came to fight in the Valley of Meḡiddo.
35.23: And the archers shot at Meleḵ Yoshiyahu. And the meleḵ said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am severely wounded.”
35.24: And his servants took him out of that chariot and put him in the second chariot that he had, and they brought him to Yerushalayim. And he died, and was buried in one of the tombs of his fathers. And all Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim were mourning for Yoshiyahu.
35.25: And Yirmeyahu lamented Yoshiyahu. And to this day all the singing men and the singing women speak of Yoshiyahu in their lamentations, and made it a law in Yisra’ĕl. And see, they are written in the Laments.
35.26: And the rest of the acts of Yoshiyahu and his kindness, according to what was written in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
35.27: and his acts from the first to the last, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.

36.1: And the people of the land took Yaho’aḥaz son of Yoshiyahu, and appointed him to reign in his father’s place in Yerushalayim.
36.2: Yaho’aḥaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Yerushalayim.
36.3: And the meleḵ of Mitsrayim turned him aside in Yerushalayim, and imposed on the land a levy of one hundred kiḵars of silver and a kiḵar of gold.
36.4: And the meleḵ of Mitsrayim made his brother Elyaqim meleḵ over Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, and changed his name to Yahoyaqim. And Neḵo took Yaho’aḥaz his brother and brought him to Mitsrayim.
36.5: Yahoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
36.6: Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel came up against him, and bound him in bronze shackles to take him away to Baḇel.
36.7: And Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar brought some of the utensils from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to Baḇel, and put them in his temple at Baḇel.
36.8: And the rest of the acts of Yahoyaqim, the abominations which he did, and what was found against him, see, they are written in the book of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah. Then Yahoyaḵin his son reigned in his place.
36.9: Yahoyaḵin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim three months and ten days. And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
36.10: And at the turn of the year Meleḵ Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sent and brought him to Baḇel, with the valuable utensils from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and made Tsiḏqiyahu, Yahoyaqim’s brother, meleḵ over Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
36.11: Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim.
36.12: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim. He did not humble himself before Yirmeyahu the naḇi, who spoke from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
36.13: And he also rebelled against Meleḵ Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, who had made him swear by Elohim, but he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
36.14: Also, all the heads of the kohenim and the people trespassed more and more, according to all the abominations of the gentiles, and they defiled the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He had qadosh in Yerushalayim.
36.15: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers sent to them, by His messengers, rising up early and sending them, for He had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place.
36.16: But they were mocking the messengers of Elohim and despising His words and scoffing at His neḇi’im, until the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 arose against His people, until there was no healing.
36.17: Therefore He brought against them the meleḵ of the Kasdites, and he slew their young men with the sword in the House of their Miqdash, and had no compassion on young man or maiden, on the aged or the weak - He gave all into his hand.
36.18: And all the utensils from the House of Elohim, great and small, and the treasures of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the treasures of the meleḵ and of his leaders, all these he brought to Baḇel.
36.19: And they burned the House of Elohim, and broke down the wall of Yerushalayim, and burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all its valuable utensils.
36.20: And those who escaped from the sword he exiled to Baḇel, where they became servants to him and his sons until the reign of the malḵuth of Paras,
36.21: in order to fill the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the mouth of Yirmeyahu, until the land had enjoyed her Shabbathoth. As long as she lay waste she kept Shabbath, until seventy years were completed.
36.22: And in the first year of Koresh meleḵ of Paras, in order to accomplish the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the mouth of Yirmeyahu, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stirred up the spirit of Koresh meleḵ of Paras, so that he called out in all his malḵuth, and also put it in writing, saying,
36.23: “Thus said Koresh meleḵ of Paras, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of the shamayim has given me all the reigns of the earth. And He has commanded me to build Him a House in Yerushalayim, which is in Yahuḏah. Whoever is among you of all His people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim be with him, and let him go up!’ ”

4.1: And he made an altar of bronze, twenty ammah long, and twenty ammah wide, and ten ammah high.
4.2: And he made the sea of cast metal, ten ammah from one rim to the other, round all about. And its height was five ammah, and a line of thirty ammah measured around it.
4.3: And figures like oxen were under it, all around it, ten to an ammah, all the way around the sea. Two rows of oxen were cast when it was cast.
4.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, and three facing west, and three facing south, and three facing east. And the sea was put upon them, and all their back parts were inward.
4.5: And it was a tophaḥ thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.
4.6: And he made ten basins, and put five on the right side and five on the left, to wash in them. In them they rinsed off what pertains to the burnt offering, but the sea was for the kohenim to wash in.
4.7: And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their ruling, and put them in the Hĕyḵal, five on the right side and five on the left.
4.8: And he made ten tables, and placed them in the Hĕyḵal, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made one hundred bowls of gold.
4.9: And he made the courtyard of the kohenim, and the great court and doors for the court. And he overlaid these doors with bronze.
4.10: And he placed the sea on the right side, eastward over against the south.
4.11: And Ḥuram made the pots and the shovels and the bowls. So Ḥuram completed doing the work that he was to do for Meleḵ Shelomoh for the House of Elohim:
4.12: the two columns and the bowl-shaped capitals that were on top of the two columns, and the two networks to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals which were on top of the columns;
4.13: and four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals that were on the columns.
4.14: And he made stands and the basins on the stands,
4.15: one sea and twelve oxen under it;
4.16: and the pots, and the shovels, and the forks. And all their vessels Ḥuram his master craftsman made of polished bronze for Meleḵ Shelomoh for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
4.17: On the plain of Yardĕn the meleḵ had them cast in clay molds, between Sukkoth and Tserĕḏathah.
4.18: And Shelomoh made so large a number of all these vessels that the weight of the bronze was not searched out.
4.19: And Shelomoh had all the furnishings made for the House of Elohim, and the altar of gold and the tables on which was the showbread,
4.20: and the lampstands with their lamps of refined gold, to burn according to Right-Ruling in front of the Speaking Place,
4.21: and the blossoms and the lamps and the snuffers of gold, of perfect gold,
4.22: and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the ladles, and the fire holders of refined gold. And the entrance to the House, its inner doors to the Most Qodesh Place, and the doors of the Hĕyḵal of the House, were of gold.

5.1: And all the work that Shelomoh had done for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was completed. And Shelomoh brought in the qodesh items of his father Dawiḏ: the silver and the gold and all the utensils. And he put them in the treasuries of the House of Elohim.
5.2: And Shelomoh assembled the elders of Yisra’ĕl and all the heads of the tribes, the chief fathers of the children of Yisra’ĕl, in Yerushalayim, to bring up the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the City of Dawiḏ, which is Tsiyon.
5.3: And all the men of Yisra’ĕl assembled to the meleḵ at the Festival, which was in the seventh month.
5.4: And all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came, and the Lĕwites took up the ark,
5.5: and they brought up the ark, the Tent of Appointment, and all the qodesh utensils that were in the Tent. The Lĕwite kohenim brought them up.
5.6: And Meleḵ Shelomoh, and all the congregation of Yisra’ĕl who were assembled to him before the ark, were slaughtering so many sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered.
5.7: And the kohenim brought in the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to its place, into the Speaking Place of the House, to the Most Qodesh Place, under the wings of the keruḇim.
5.8: For the keruḇim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the keruḇim covered over the ark and its poles.
5.9: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles of the ark were seen from in front of the Speaking Place, but they were not seen from outside. And they are there to this day.
5.10: There was naught in the ark but the two tablets which Mosheh put there at Ḥorĕḇ, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made a Covenant with the children of Yisra’ĕl, when they came out of Mitsrayim.
5.11: And it came to be when the kohenim came out of the Most Qodesh Place - for all the kohenim who were present had qadosh themselves, there was none to watch by division -
5.12: and the Lĕwite singers, all those of Asaph and Hĕman and Yeḏuthun, with their sons and their brothers, stood at the east end of the altar, dressed in white linen, having cymbals and harps and lyres, and with them one hundred and twenty kohenim sounding with trumpets.
5.13: Then it came to be, as the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets, and with cymbals, and with instruments of song, and giving praise to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “For He is good, for His kindness is everlasting,” that the House, the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, was filled with a cloud,
5.14: and the kohenim were unable to stand and perform the service because of the cloud, for the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 filled the House of Elohim.

6.1: Then Shelomoh said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said He would dwell in the thick cloud.
6.2: “But I have built You an exalted house, and a place for You to dwell in forever.”
6.3: And the meleḵ turned around and baraḵ all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, while all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl stood.
6.4: And he said, “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, who has filled with His hands what He spoke with His mouth to my father Dawiḏ, saying,
6.5: ‘From the day that I brought My people out of the land of Mitsrayim, I have chosen no city from any tribe of Yisra’ĕl in which to build a House for My Name to be there, nor did I choose any man to be a leader over My people Yisra’ĕl.
6.6: ‘But I have chosen Yerushalayim, for My Name to be there. And I have chosen Dawiḏ to be over My people Yisra’ĕl.’
6.7: “And it was in the heart of my father Dawiḏ to build a House for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
6.8: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to my father Dawiḏ, ‘Because it was in your heart to build a House for My Name, you did well in that it was in your heart.
6.9: ‘But you do not build the House, for your son who comes forth from your loins, he builds the House for My Name.’
6.10: “Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has established His word which He spoke, and I have been raised up instead of my father Dawiḏ, and sit on the throne of Yisra’ĕl, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 promised. And I have built the House for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
6.11: “And there I have placed the ark, in which is the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He made with the children of Yisra’ĕl.”
6.12: And he stood before the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in front of all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, and spread out his hands -
6.13: for Shelomoh had made a bronze platform five ammah long, and five ammah broad, and three ammah high, and had put it in the midst of the court. And he stood on it, and knelt down on his knees before all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, and spread out his hands toward the shamayim -
6.14: and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, there is no Elohim in the shamayim or on earth like You, guarding the Covenant and kindness with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,
6.15: who has guarded what You promised Your servant Dawiḏ my father. Indeed, You have both spoken with Your mouth and have filled it with Your hand, as it is this day.
6.16: “And now, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, guard what You promised Your servant Dawiḏ my father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours before Me, sitting on the throne of Yisra’ĕl - only, if your sons guard their way, to walk in My Torah as you have walked before Me.’
6.17: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, let Your word come true which You have spoken to Your servant Dawiḏ.
6.18: “For is it true: Elohim dwells with men on the earth! See, the shamayim and the shamayim of the shamayim are unable to contain You, how much less this House which I have built!
6.19: “Yet, shall You turn to the prayer of Your servant and his supplication, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which Your servant is praying before You?
6.20: “For Your eyes to be open toward this House day and night, toward the place You have said to put Your Name there, to listen to the prayer which Your servant prays toward this place.
6.21: “And shall You give heed to the supplications of Your servant and of Your people Yisra’ĕl, when they pray toward this place, and hear from Your dwelling place, in the shamayim, and shall hear and forgive?
6.22: “If anyone sins against his neighbor, and he has lifted up an oath on him, to cause him to swear, and comes and swears before Your altar in this House,
6.23: then hear in the shamayim, and act, and rightly rule Your servants, repaying the wicked by bringing his way on his own head, and declare right the righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.
6.24: “And if Your people Yisra’ĕl are smitten before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they shall turn back and confess Your Name, and pray and make supplication before You in this House,
6.25: then hear in the shamayim and forgive the sin of Your people Yisra’ĕl, and bring them back to the land which You gave to them and their fathers.
6.26: “When the shamayim are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they shall pray toward this place and confess Your Name, and turn from their sin because You afflict them,
6.27: then hear in the shamayim, and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Yisra’ĕl - for You teach them the good Way in which they should walk - and shall send rain on Your land which You have given to Your people as an inheritance.
6.28: “When there is scarcity of food in the land; when there is pestilence or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers; when their enemies distress them in the land of their cities; any plague or any sickness;
6.29: whatever prayer, whatever supplication is made by anyone, or by all Your people Yisra’ĕl, when, each one knows his own plague and his own grief, and spreads out his hands to this house,
6.30: then hear from the shamayim Your dwelling place, and forgive, and give to everyone according to all his ways, whose heart You know - for You alone know the hearts of the sons of men -
6.31: so that they revere You, to walk in Your Ways as long as they live in the land which You gave to our fathers.
6.32: “Also, concerning a foreigner, who is not of Your people Yisra’ĕl, but who comes from a far land for the sake of Your great Name and Your strong hand and Your outstretched arm, when they come and pray in this House,
6.33: then hear from the shamayim Your dwelling place, and do according to all which the foreigner calls to You for, so that all the people of the earth know Your Name and revere You, as do Your people Yisra’ĕl, and to know that this House which I have built is called by Your Name.
6.34: “When Your people go out to battle against their enemies, in the way that You send them, and they shall pray to You toward this city which You have chosen and toward the House which I have built for Your Name,
6.35: then shall You hear from the shamayim their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause?
6.36: “When they sin against You - for there is no one who does not sin - and You become enraged with them and give them to the enemy, and they take them captive to a land far or near,
6.37: and they shall turn back unto their heart, in the land where they have been taken captive, and shall turn, and make supplication to You in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have acted wickedly, and have done wickedness,’
6.38: and when they return to You with all their heart and with all their being in the land of their captivity, where they have taken them captive, and they shall pray toward their land which You gave to their fathers, and the city which You have chosen, and toward the House which I have built for Your Name,
6.39: then shall You hear from the shamayim, Your dwelling place, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause, and forgive Your people who have sinned against You?
6.40: “Now, my Elohim, I pray, let Your eyes be open and let Your ears be attentive to the prayer of this place.
6.41: “And now, arise, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength. Let Your kohenim, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, be robed with deliverance, and let Your kind ones rejoice in goodness.
6.42: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, do not turn away the face of Your anointed; remember the kind acts of Your servant Dawiḏ.”

7.1: And when Shelomoh had ended praying, fire came down from the shamayim and consumed the burnt offering and the slaughterings. And the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 filled the House.
7.2: And the kohenim were unable to enter the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had filled the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.3: And all the children of Yisra’ĕl saw how the fire came down, and the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the House, and they bowed their faces to the ground on the pavement, and did obeisance and gave thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “For He is good, for His kindness is everlasting.”
7.4: And the meleḵ and all the people were making offerings before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.5: And Meleḵ Shelomoh made an offering of twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the meleḵ and all the people dedicated the House of Elohim.
7.6: And the kohenim were standing over their duties, and the Lĕwites with instruments of the song to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which Meleḵ Dawiḏ had made to give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “For His kindness is everlasting,” whenever Dawiḏ praised by their hand. And the kohenim were blowing trumpets before them, and all Yisra’ĕl were standing.
7.7: And Shelomoh qadosh the middle of the courtyard that was in front of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for there he made burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Shelomoh had made was not able to contain the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat.
7.8: And Shelomoh at that time observed the Festival seven days, and all Yisra’ĕl with him, a very great assembly from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi of Mitsrayim.
7.9: And on the eighth day they held an assembly, for they performed the dedication of the altar seven days, and the Festival seven days.
7.10: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, rejoicing and glad of heart for the goodness that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had done for Dawiḏ, and for Shelomoh, and for His people Yisra’ĕl.
7.11: Thus Shelomoh finished the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the meleḵ’s house. And all that came into the heart of Shelomoh to do in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in his own house, he prosperously executed.
7.12: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to Shelomoh by night, and said to him, “I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place for Myself as a House of slaughtering.
7.13: “If I shut up the shamayim and there is no rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among My people,
7.14: and My people upon whom My Name is called, shall humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their evil ways, then I shall hear from the shamayim, and forgive their sin and heal their land.
7.15: “Now, My eyes are open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
7.16: “And now, I have chosen and qadosh this house for My Name to be there forever. And My eyes and My heart shall always be there.
7.17: “And you, if you walk before Me as your father Dawiḏ walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and if you guard My Laws and My Right-Rulings,
7.18: then I shall establish the throne of your malḵuth, as I covenanted with Dawiḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours as ruler in Yisra’ĕl.’
7.19: “But if you turn away and forsake My Laws and My Commands which I have put before you, and shall go and serve other mighty ones, and bow yourself to them,
7.20: then I shall pluck them from My land, which I have given them, and this House which I have qadosh for My Name I shall cast out of My sight and make it to be a proverb and a mockery among all peoples.
7.21: “And this House, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished and say, ‘Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 done thus to this land and this House?’
7.22: “Then they shall say, ‘Because they forsook 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, and embraced other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to them and served them, therefore He has brought all this evil on them.’ ”

8.1: And it came to be at the end of twenty years, that Shelomoh had built the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and his own house.
8.2: As to the cities which Ḥuram had given to Shelomoh, Shelomoh had built them, and he settled the children of Yisra’ĕl there.
8.3: And Shelomoh went to Ḥamath Tsoḇah and seized it.
8.4: And he built Taḏmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities which he built in Ḥamath.
8.5: And he built Upper Bĕyth Ḥoron and Lower Bĕyth Ḥoron, cities of defense, with walls, gates, and bars,
8.6: also Ba’alath and all the storage cities that Shelomoh had, and all the chariot cities and the cities of the cavalry, and all that Shelomoh desired to build in Yerushalayim, and in Leḇanon, and in all the land of his rule.
8.7: All the people who were left of the Ḥittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Ḥiwwites, and the Yeḇusites, who were not of Yisra’ĕl -
8.8: their descendants who were left in the land after them, whom the children of Yisra’ĕl did not destroy - from these Shelomoh raised compulsory labor, as it is to this day.
8.9: And Shelomoh did not make slaves of the children of Yisra’ĕl for his work, but they were men of battle, and chiefs of his officers, and commanders of his chariots, and his cavalry.
8.10: And these were the chiefs of the officials of Meleḵ Shelomoh: two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.
8.11: And Shelomoh brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the City of Dawiḏ to the house he had built for her, for he said, “My wife does not dwell in the house of Dawiḏ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, for where the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has come, is qodesh.”
8.12: Then Shelomoh offered burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which he had built before the porch,
8.13: even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the command of Mosheh, for the Shabbathoth, and for the New Moons, and for the Appointed Times three times a year: the Festival of Matstsoth, and the Festival of Shaḇuoth, and the Festival of Sukkoth.
8.14: And according to the ruling of Dawiḏ his father, he appointed the divisions of the kohenim for their service, the Lĕwites for their duties, to praise and serve before the kohenim, as the duty of each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for so was the command of Dawiḏ the man of Elohim.
8.15: And they did not turn aside from the command of the meleḵ to the kohenim and Lĕwites concerning any matter or concerning the treasuries.
8.16: And all the work of Shelomoh was prepared from the day of the foundation of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 until it was completed. And the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was perfected.
8.17: Then Shelomoh went to Etsyon Geḇer and Ĕyloth on the seacoast, in the land of Eḏom.
8.18: And Ḥuram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, and servants who knew the sea. And they went with the servants of Shelomoh to Ophir, and took four hundred and fifty kiḵars of gold from there, and brought it to Meleḵ Shelomoh.

9.1: And the malkah of Sheḇa heard of the report of Shelomoh, and came to Yerushalayim to try Shelomoh with hard questions, with a very great company, and camels bearing spices, and much gold, and precious stones. And she came to Shelomoh, and she spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
9.2: And Shelomoh answered all her questions. And there was no matter hidden for Shelomoh which he did not make known to her.
9.3: And the malkah of Sheḇa saw the wisdom of Shelomoh, and the house that he had built,
9.4: and the food on his table, and the seating of his servants, and the service of his waiters and their attire, and his cupbearers and their attire, and his burnt offerings that he offered up in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and there was no more spirit in her.
9.5: Then she said to the meleḵ, “True was the word I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
9.6: “But I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And see, I have not been told the half of the greatness of your wisdom! You exceed the report which I heard.
9.7: “Ashrĕ are your men and ashrĕ are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
9.8: “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who delighted in you, to put you on His throne to be meleḵ for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim! Because your Elohim has loved Yisra’ĕl, to establish them forever, therefore He made you meleḵ over them, to do right-ruling and righteousness.”
9.9: And she gave the meleḵ one hundred and twenty kiḵars of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones. And there has not been any spices such as those the malkah of Sheḇa gave to Meleḵ Shelomoh.
9.10: And also, the servants of Ḥuram and the servants of Shelomoh, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum wood and precious stones.
9.11: And the meleḵ made stairs of the algum wood for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and for the meleḵ’s house, also lyres and harps for singers. And there was never seen the like of them before in the land of Yahuḏah.
9.12: And Meleḵ Shelomoh gave to the malkah of Sheḇa all she desired, whatever she asked, besides that which she had brought to the meleḵ. And she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants.
9.13: And the weight of gold that came to Shelomoh yearly was six hundred and sixty-six kiḵars of gold,
9.14: besides that which the merchants and traders brought. And all the melaḵim of Araḇia and governors of the land were bringing gold and silver to Shelomoh.
9.15: And Meleḵ Shelomoh made two hundred large shields of beaten gold - six hundred pieces of beaten gold went into each shield,
9.16: and three hundred shields of beaten gold - three hundred pieces of gold went unto each shield. And the meleḵ put them in the House of the Forest of Leḇanon.
9.17: And the meleḵ, made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with clean gold,
9.18: and six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne; and there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests.
9.19: And twelve lions were standing there, one on each side of the six steps. The like of it was not in any reign.
9.20: And all the drinking vessels of Meleḵ Shelomoh were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Leḇanon were of refined gold - silver was reckoned of little value in the days of Shelomoh.
9.21: For the meleḵ’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Ḥuram. Once in three years the ships of Tarshish came, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, apes, and baboons.
9.22: And Meleḵ Shelomoh became greater than all the melaḵim of the earth in riches and wisdom.
9.23: And all the melaḵim of the earth sought the presence of Shelomoh to hear his wisdom, which Elohim had put in his heart.
9.24: And each man brought his present: objects of silver, and objects of gold, and garments, and armor, and spices, horses and mules, the matter of a year by year.
9.25: And Shelomoh had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the meleḵ at Yerushalayim.
9.26: And he ruled over all the melaḵim from the River to the land of the Pelishtites, as far as the border of Mitsrayim.
9.27: And the meleḵ made silver in Yerushalayim as the stones, and he made cedar trees as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country.
9.28: And they were bringing horses to Shelomoh from Mitsrayim and from all lands.
9.29: And the rest of the acts of Shelomoh, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the naḇi, and in the neḇuah of Aḥiyahu the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat?
9.30: And Shelomoh reigned in Yerushalayim over all Yisra’ĕl forty years.
9.31: So Shelomoh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Dawiḏ his father. And Reḥaḇ’am his son reigned in his place.
